papers.abstract: CDK4/6 inhibitors have reshaped treatment for hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, but resistance frequently emerges and may interact with metastatic phenotypic evolution. We developed an integrated resistance-discordance framework and explored its clinical interpretability in invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) with gastric metastasis. Public MSK-INK4 (cBioPortal study ID: breast_ink4_msk_2021) and MBCproject (brca_mbcproject_wagle_2017) cohorts were curated for HR+/HER2-negative disease. A five-module CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance score (0-5) was constructed from predefined mutation and copy-number events. In MBCproject RNA-seq samples, single-sample gene-set enrichment analysis quantified proliferation and estrogen-response activity. Discordance burden was defined as z(proliferation score) minus z(ER score), using primary tumors as the reference. Three institutional IDC gastric-metastasis cases were projected onto the framework for interpretability but not inferential testing. Seventy HR+/HER2-negative MBCproject samples and 1116 deduplicated MSK-INK4 metastatic samples were analyzed. MBCproject metastases had higher resistance scores than primary tumors (P = 0.001), whereas metastatic scores were similar between MBCproject and MSK-INK4 (P = 0.202). Metastases showed higher proliferation activity (P = 0.014) and a trend toward lower ER activity (P = 0.071). The high-resistance/high-discordance quadrant was enriched for PI3K-axis events (OR = 16.52; P = 0.034), chromatin-remodeling loss-of-function events (OR = 12.47; P = 0.001), and cell-cycle/RB-axis events (OR = 9.03; P = 0.001). Among the three IDC gastric-metastasis cases, two available gastric NGS profiles mapped to predefined resistance modules, and the case with increased gastric Ki-67 showed the strongest IHC-adapted discordance and projected toward the high-resistance/high-discordance phenotype. Coupling resistance-associated genomic events with metastatic phenotype discordance may provide a clinically interpretable lens for HR+/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and for rare IDC gastric-metastasis presentations.

papers.abstract: The aims of this study were to explore the longitudinal trajectories of core symptoms in survivors with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and to analyze their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and unmet supportive care needs. This longitudinal study enrolled 271 HCC survivors undergoing TACE in China. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed at three time points-24 h (T1), 7 days (T2), and 1 month (T3) post-TACE-using four validated instruments: the MD Anderson Symptom Inventory-Chinese Version (MDASI-C), the Tumor Symptom Measure for Primary Liver Cancer (TSM-PLC), the Quality of Life Instrument for Liver Cancer (QOL-LC V2.0), and the Short Form of Survivors' Unmet Needs Scale (SF-SUNS). Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to extract discrete symptom clusters, and network analysis was used to calculate strength centrality (rs)-an index quantifying the sum of absolute edge weights connecting each symptom to all others-to identify core symptoms. Five symptom clusters were identified at T1: Fatigue-Cognitive, Post-embolization, Somatic, Emotional, and Hepatobiliary-Specific. The Post-embolization cluster was present only at T1, whereas the remaining four clusters persisted at T2 and T3. However, the core symptom shifted over time: nausea at T1 (rs = 1.154), lack of appetite at T2 (rs = 1.229), and sadness at T3 (rs = 1.107). HRQoL was lowest at T1, improved at T2, and declined at T3, with all pairwise comparisons significant (all p < 0.001). Unmet needs were highest at T3, with all time-point differences significant (all p < 0.001). The largest gaps were observed in information provision, care continuity, and emotional support. Greater symptom severity was significantly associated with poorer HRQoL at all time points (all p < 0.01). During the first month post-TACE, the sequence of core symptoms transitioned from nausea to lack of appetite and then to sadness, suggesting time-specific supportive care strategies-including antiemetic prophylaxis, nutritional support, and psychosocial care. Routine assessment of unmet needs may help reduce symptom burden and optimize long-term HRQoL for these survivors.

papers.abstract: Clozapine is the gold standard for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS). It requires strict monitoring of full blood count (FBC), due to the risk of neutropenia and agranulocytosis. AB is a woman in her mid-40s with TRS, diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast. She was commenced on a chemotherapy regimen of docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab. Four days after the initial infusion, AB developed neutropenia with an absolute neutrophil count of 0.2 × 109/L. In accordance with local protocols and discussion with the Clozapine Patient Monitoring Service (CPMS), clozapine was immediately discontinued. Two weeks after clozapine cessation, AB displayed catatonic symptoms characterised by mutism, posturing, and automatic obedience, scoring 27 on the Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale (BFCRS). A positive lorazepam challenge confirmed the diagnosis of clozapine-withdrawal catatonia. Despite regular high-dose benzodiazepines and treatment with antipsychotics, AB's presentation continued to deteriorate, characterised by prominent delusions and hallucinations, impeding oncological treatment. AB was seen extensively by liaison psychiatry and treated with high-dose typical and atypical antipsychotics; however, she failed to respond adequately to treatment. Given AB's extensive previous history of management on clozapine without previous haematological disturbance and ongoing decline in mental state, coupled with the timeline of symptoms 4 days after the administration of chemotherapy agents associated with neutropenia, namely, carboplatin, the decision was taken to reinstate clozapine. Following titration of clozapine and transfer to a specialist psychiatric unit, AB's symptoms resolved rapidly, allowing for the successful completion of chemotherapy. Carboplatin was omitted in subsequent cycles, with no further episodes of neutropenia. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of neutropenia in psychiatric patients on clozapine, who are also undergoing treatment for comorbid medical conditions. The presence of neutropenia in clozapine patients may lead to diagnostic overshadowing and delay the diagnosis of the underlying cause of neutropenia, resulting in delays to treatment as well as unnecessary cessation of clozapine and risk of relapse. Furthermore, this case highlights the risk of catatonia associated with the withdrawal of clozapine and the importance of its rapid identification and management. Clinicians should consider differing aetiologies of neutropenia in clozapine patients, especially those undergoing chemotherapy. Furthermore, clinicians should be skilled in recognising catatonia and initiating prompt treatment.

papers.abstract: Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed-large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space-Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free after nodule localization: an SSM3D stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an OrthoLoRA stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset (n = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms. A standard full-volume nnU-Net v2 baseline reached 88.6% ± 1.0% Dice on the same QIN folds, still below HSV-Net. On an independent LIDC-IDRI benchmark with expert volumetric consensus masks (186 patients/294 nodules; patient-level 5-fold CV within LIDC, not QIN→LIDC transfer), HSV-Net achieved 87.8% ± 1.1% Dice and 83.6% ± 1.3% Boundary F1, outperforming full-volume nnU-Net (87.1% ± 1.0% Dice). LUNA16 was retained only as a proxy size/localization check with diameter-matched spherical references, not as contour external validation.

papers.abstract: Solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) is an uncommon mesenchymal spindle cell neoplasm (incidence ~1.4 per million). Although most SFT occur in the thoracic cavity, they can also arise in the retroperitoneum, pelvis, head, and neck. While the majority exhibit benign behavior, approximately 5% are associated with paraneoplastic syndromes, most notably Doege-Potter syndrome (DPS). DPS is characterized by non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia (NICTH) resulting from tumor hypersecretion of high-molecular-weight insulin-like growth factor 2 (IGF2), which saturates insulin and IGF receptors causing refractory, life-threatening hypoglycemia. Due to nonspecific presentation and low incidence, DPS secondary to pelvic SFT is frequently misdiagnosed, underscoring the need for heightened clinical awareness. A 56-year-old man presented to the neurology department with acute loss of consciousness, aphasia, and urinary incontinence. He had a 3-year history of hypertension but no diabetes mellitus. Initial laboratory tests showed a blood glucose of 4.76 mmol/L; however, during hospitalization, he developed recurrent severe hypoglycemia, with a nadir glucose of 1.6 mmol/L. Further biochemical evaluation during fasting hypoglycemia revealed undetectable insulin (<0.2 mIU/L) and low C-peptide (0.14 ng/mL). Contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT demonstrated a 17.8 cm heterogeneously enhancing pelvic mass causing bladder compression and left ureteral displacement. The patient declined preoperative biopsy. Preoperative euglycemia was maintained with continuous intravenous dextrose infusion, and open en bloc surgical resection was performed. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry (positive for STAT6, CD34, and CD99; Ki-67 8%) confirmed an atypical solitary fibrous tumor. Postoperatively, hypoglycemic symptoms resolved completely, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 6 without further hypoglycemic episodes. Pelvic SFT with DPS frequently presents with recurrent hypoglycemia or altered consciousness rather than local compressive symptoms. Early recognition of non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia (NICTH) and prompt cross-sectional imaging are essential for accurate diagnosis. Complete surgical resection is definitive and results in full resolution of hypoglycemia. Given the unpredictable biological behavior of SFT, long-term follow-up is essential. Heightened clinical awareness may improve diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: The transportability of models for postoperative high-volume cervical nodal disease in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) and the incremental predictive value of molecular variables remain uncertain. We developed models in the public Deyang cohort (521 patients; 90 events) and performed geographic external validation in the independent Liaocheng cohort (193 patients; 73 events). The outcome was >5 pathologically confirmed metastatic cervical lymph nodes. Five algorithms were compared using repeated stratified nested cross-validation with a prespecified 10-variable postoperative feature set. Ridge logistic regression (C = 0.1) was selected and applied without refitting. Paired comparisons of 8-variable clinicopathological and 10-variable clinicopathological-molecular models assessed the incremental value of high-risk co-mutation status and mutation count in both cohorts. Internal validation yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.795 (95% CI, 0.745-0.842), average precision (AP) of 0.497 (0.406-0.598), and Brier score of 0.115 (0.098-0.134). External AUROC was 0.752 (0.678-0.821), AP 0.601 (0.498-0.728), and Brier score 0.217 (0.180-0.254). Observed and mean predicted risks were 37.8% and 23.9%, respectively; the observed-to-expected ratio was 1.582 (1.319-1.860) and the weak-calibration slope was 0.831 (0.542-1.191). At the prespecified threshold of 0.158, sensitivity was 0.795 and specificity 0.600. Net benefit was 0.254 for the model and 0.261 for classifying all patients as high risk (difference, -0.008; 95% CI, -0.051 to 0.033). External paired differences after adding molecular variables were +0.002 for AUROC (-0.005 to 0.010), -0.002 for AP (-0.016 to 0.010), -0.001 for Brier score (-0.002 to 0.000), and +0.009 for net benefit (-0.003 to 0.026). The model retained moderate discrimination across centers but underestimated absolute risk and did not demonstrate a net benefit advantage over classifying all patients as high risk at the prespecified threshold. High-risk co-mutation status and mutation count showed no clear incremental predictive value. Further validation with standardized lymph-node assessment and patient outcomes is required before clinical application.

papers.abstract: The global burden of liver cancer has been increasing over recent decades, whereas the incidence in Switzerland has remained relatively stable. This study assessed long-term trends in incidence, mortality, and 1- and 5-year relative survival of primary liver cancer in the Swiss canton of Zurich from 1980 to 2022, stratified by sex and age. This population-based retrospective analysis included all primary liver cancer cases diagnosed in the canton of Zurich and registered in the Cancer Registry of the cantons of Zurich, Zug, Schaffhausen and Schwyz between 1980 and 2022. Mortality data were obtained from the Federal Statistical Office. Cases were classified according to ICD-O-3 topography and morphology and, from 2003 onward, TNM stage. Age-standardised incidence and mortality rates were calculated using the 1976 European standard population. Temporal trends were analysed using Joinpoint regression and reported as Average Annual Percentage Changes (AAPCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Relative survival was estimated using the Ederer II method and standardised according to international standards. Among 3866 incident cases, 71.3% were hepatocellular carcinomas and 70.7% occurred in men. Overall age-standardised incidence remained stable in both men (AAPC -0.1%, 95% CI -0.6 to 0.3%) and women (-0.2%, -0.9% to 0.4%). However, incidence increased significantly among individuals younger than 65 years, particularly in women (AAPC 2.3%, 1.3%-3.3%) and men (1.2%, 0.6%-1.9%). Mortality remained broadly stable in men and increased modestly in women. One- and five-year relative survival improved substantially, from 13.8% and 3.5% in 1980-1999 to 53.9% and 25.8% in 2016-2022, respectively. Improvements were greater in men than women. These findings reflect major advances in liver cancer diagnosis and treatment over the past four decades. Continued prevention, targeted screening of high-risk groups, and epidemiological monitoring remain important.

papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) continues to present therapeutic challenges because of pathway redundancy and treatment resistance, underscoring the need for multi-target and systems-level strategies. Baicalein (BA), a flavonoid metabolite from Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, shows antitumor potential, yet integrative and immune-related evaluations of BA in LUAD remain limited. We integrated network analyses with TCGA-LUAD transcriptomics, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), network topology, GO/KEGG enrichment, bulk RNA-seq-based immune-infiltration estimation (CIBERSORT), molecular docking, and clinical association analysis (GEPIA2/HPA). Cell viability was assessed in A549 cells​ using the CCK-8 assay, and AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression were further examined experimentally by western blot analysis. A total of 117 candidate BA-LUAD overlapping targets were identified, and six candidate hub genes (EGFR, AKT1, TP53, BCL2, HIF1A, and ESR1) were prioritized. Enrichment analyses suggested that the candidate network was associated with oncogenic signaling and stress-response programs, particularly PI3K-AKT/MAPK signaling, ROS-related processes, apoptosis, and p53 signaling. CCK-8 assays showed that BA reduced A549 cell viability in vitro, with IC50 values of 54.93 μM at 24 h and 22.83 μM at 48 h. Among the prioritized candidates, AKT1 and BCL2 were selected for focused experimental assessment in A549 cells. BA treatment reduced AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression in A549 cells, whereas total AKT1 remained largely unchanged. HIF1A expression showed broad associations with computationally estimated immune-cell fractions and poorer overall survival. These findings prioritize a BA-associated candidate network in LUAD involving kinase signaling, apoptosis-related regulation, oxidative-stress responses, and immune-microenvironment associations. The CCK-8 results support an inhibitory effect of BA on A549 cell viability in vitro, and the observed changes in AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression provide focused experimental support for selected components of the candidate network; further in vitro and in vivo studies are required to validate biological relevance and translational potential.

papers.abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are distinctive toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and have been reported to correlate with clinical outcomes in several cancers. However, whether this association also exists in patients with esophageal cancer (EC) receiving ICIs remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between irAEs and clinical outcomes in this population. This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated the association between irAEs and progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), or disease control rate (DCR). Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled for PFS and OS, whereas odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were pooled for ORR and DCR using random-effects models. Between-study heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), sensitivity analyses, publication bias, prespecified subgroup analyses, and immortal-time bias were also assessed. 14 studies involving 1, 546 patients were included. The occurrence of irAEs was associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.31-0.63), OS (HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.46-0.64), ORR (OR, 4.00; 95% CI, 1.58-10.12), and DCR (OR, 3.85; 95% CI, 2.40-6.20). The 95% PIs were 0.16-1.24, 0.44-0.66, 0.19-82.57, and 1.42-10.44 for PFS, OS, ORR, and DCR, respectively, crossing the null value for PFS and ORR. Subgroup estimates were generally similar in direction but remained exploratory. No eligible survival estimates using landmark or time-varying approaches were available for the comparison between patients with and without irAEs. In patients with EC receiving ICIs, the occurrence of irAEs may be a prognostic marker of favorable outcomes. However, wide PIs for PFS and ORR indicate that these associations may vary across future studies and immortal time bias may overestimate survival associations. This observational evidence derives mainly from East Asian patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and is primarily applicable to these patients. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and require prospective validation. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261346294.

papers.abstract: Colon cancer is a leading global malignancy influenced by genetic, environmental, and microbial factors. This study integrates ecological theories, including Hubbell's neutral theory, augmented by Ning et al.'s (2019, PNAS) stochasticity analysis framework, and classic niche theory, to assess the contributions of stochastic colonization and deterministic niche selection in shaping microbiome assembly and dynamics in colon cancer tissues. Specialist species were identified using Levins' niche breadth analysis. By reanalyzing the datasets from Nejman et al., including 22 normal adjacent tissue (NT) and 22 primary tumor (PT) samples, we find: (i) deterministic niche selection appears to dominate community assembly and diversity maintenance in both NT and PT microbiomes, as demonstrated by the normalized stochasticity ratio (NSR: 0.267 for NT, 0.287 for PT; both below 0.5; Wilcoxon PT>NT, p=0.027). Only 18.2% NT and 27.3% PT samples fit the neutral model, confirming stochastic drift plays a limited role and niche selection predominates in structuring tissue microbiomes. (ii) Through niche breadth analysis, we identified 106 specialist species, of which 14 are known CRC-associated taxa, including Fusobacterium nucleatum, Escherichia coli, Enterococcus faecalis, and Peptostreptococcus anaerobius. These species have established roles in inflammation, genotoxicity, immune modulation, and chemoresistance. (iii) These findings suggest that deterministic niche-based selection, rather than stochastic colonization, appears to govern microbial community assembly in colon cancer tissues. (iv) We postulate that the tumor microenvironment imposes biochemical filters-including hypoxia, lactate accumulation, and altered pH-that select for specialist species capable of adapting to these conditions. (v) While the sample size is modest and validation in independent cohorts is needed, our study demonstrates an integrative framework for understanding colon cancer microbiome dynamics. We propose testable hypotheses for future research: (i) specialist species abundance may correlate with tumor stage or patient survival; (2) depletion of specialists may alter tumor progression in preclinical models; and (3) hybrid neutral-niche models may better fit larger longitudinal datasets. By integrating ecological theory with microbiome research, this study offers insights into the forces driving microbial community assembly in tumor tissues and highlights potential targets for microbiome-based diagnostics and therapeutics.

papers.abstract: Cysteine-rich angiogenic inducer 61 (CYR61), a matricellular protein, has been implicated in gastric cancer aggressiveness through activation of integrin-mediated NF-κB signaling; however, effective pharmacological strategies targeting this axis remain limited. Cyclopiane, a bioactive small-molecule compound, has shown potential anti-tumor activity, but its role and underlying mechanisms in gastric cancer have not been fully elucidated. This study aimed to investigate whether Cyclopiane suppresses gastric cancer invasion and angiogenesis via modulation of the CYR61/αvβ3 integrin/NF-κB signaling pathway. Human gastric cancer cell lines AGS and MKN45 were treated with increasing concentrations of Cyclopiane. Cell viability was assessed using MTT assays, while invasive capacity was evaluated using Matrigel-coated Transwell assays. TUNEL staining was used to assess changes in apoptosis in tumor cells. The expression of invasion-, angiogenesis-, and inflammation-related proteins was analyzed by Western blot (WB) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Transcriptomic profiling of AGS cells treated with Cyclopiane versus vehicle control was performed to identify differentially expressed genes and enriched signaling pathways. CYR61 overexpression was achieved via adeno-associated virus (AAV-CYR61), with its pathway involvement further validated using integrin αvβ3 antagonists. The conventional anticancer drug 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) was employed to compare Cyclopiane's therapeutic effects. In vivo experiments utilized a nude mouse xenograft model to evaluate changes in tumor growth, angiogenesis, and inflammatory responses following Cyclopiane treatment. We found that Cyclopiane significantly reduced cell viability, invasive capacity of AGS and MKN45 cells and promoted apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner, with its high-dose effects comparable to those of 5-FU. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that Cyclopiane downregulated CCN1/CYR61, ITGAV and ITGB3 expression, with pathway enrichment identifying integrin signaling, ECM-receptor interaction, focal adhesion and NF-κB pathways as the top modulated terms. In vivo experiments demonstrated that Cyclopiane significantly inhibited tumor growth and progression. Both in vivo and in vitro studies showed Cyclopiane significantly downregulated vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2), and MMP-9 expression while inhibiting integrin αvβ3 expression and NF-κB activation, as evidenced by reduced phosphorylation levels of p65 and IκBα. Overexpression of CYR61 partially reversed the inhibition of invasion, angiogenic factor production, and NF-κB signaling mediated by Cyclopiane. The αvβ3/αvβ5 integrin antagonist Cilengitide also exhibited tumor-suppressive effects, and the co-treatment of Cyclopiane with Cilengitide achieved the strongest tumor-suppressive effect. These findings suggest that modulation of the CYR61/integrin/NF-κB signaling axis contributes, at least in part, to the anti-invasive and anti-angiogenic effects of Cyclopiane in preclinical gastric cancer models. Further studies are required to establish its molecular target specificity, safety, selectivity, and translational potential.

papers.abstract: Background Prophylactic gastrostomy is widely used during definitive chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced head and neck cancer (LAHNC), yet some patients remain tube-dependent long after treatment. Whether prolonged dependence carries prognostic weight of its own, or simply mirrors tumour burden and performance status, is unclear. We examined predictors of time to feeding-tube independence and the association between persistent dependence and overall survival (OS). Methods We reviewed 213 consecutive patients with LAHNC treated at a single institution (2015–2022) with definitive chemoradiotherapy to 70 Gy and prophylactic PEG/RIG placement. Nine patients with an inconsistent extraction date were excluded, leaving 204. Time to independence was analysed with Kaplan–Meier estimates and cause-specific multivariable Cox regression, treating death as a competing risk, with a Fine–Gray sensitivity model. Dosimetric variables and baseline Karnofsky performance status (KPS) were modelled continuously. To avoid immortal-time bias, OS was assessed with landmark analyses at 3, 6 and 12 months. Patients were classified by tube status at each landmark, with adjustment for KPS, T and N classification, smoking history and age. Results Median time to independence was 3.2 months. Any smoking history predicted slower independence (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.42–0.84; p=0.004), and higher KPS predicted faster independence (HR 1.02 per point, 95% CI 1.01–1.04; p=0.006). Higher middle pharyngeal constrictor dose was associated with slower recovery (HR 0.98 per Gy, 95% CI 0.96–1.00; p=0.048), and oral cavity dose showed a similar trend (p=0.067). In unadjusted landmark analyses, patients still dependent had worse OS at 6 months (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.01–3.13) and 12 months (HR 2.53, 95% CI 1.30–4.91). After adjustment, the association was attenuated and non-significant at 3 months (aHR 1.35, 95% CI 0.76–2.42) and 6 months (aHR 1.48, 95% CI 0.81–2.70), but persisted at 12 months (aHR 2.20, 95% CI 1.05–4.58; p=0.036). Conclusions Early tube dependence largely reflects baseline disease burden and performance status. Dependence persisting to one year, however, identifies patients with worse survival that these factors do not explain, and they may merit closer follow-up. Smoking history and middle constrictor dose are potentially modifiable contributors to slower recovery, supporting structured smoking-cessation care and dysphagia-optimised planning. Prospective validation is warranted.

papers.abstract: Background Perineural invasion (PNI) is an aggressive biological feature of colorectal cancer (CRC) driven by active crosstalk between tumor cells, Schwann cells, and the neural microenvironment. Although PNI is associated with recurrence, distant metastasis, and chemoresistance, its pathologic diagnosis is constrained by sampling limitations and inter-observer variability, and direct patient-level evidence linking PNI to the cellular sensitivity of specific cytotoxic agents such as capecitabine is lacking. Methods We performed a retrospective dual-cohort study of 724 patients with histologically confirmed colorectal adenocarcinoma who underwent R0 resection between January 2024 and August 2025 at a tertiary cancer center in China. Cohort A (n = 430) was used to develop and validate a clinicopathologic nomogram for PNI through LASSO regression, multivariable logistic modeling, bootstrap-corrected internal validation, and internal hold-out validation. Discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), mean absolute error (MAE), Hosmer–Lemeshow test, and decision curve analysis. The association between PNI and distant metastasis was examined in the full cohort by multivariable logistic regression. Cohort B (n = 390) underwent ATP-based in vitro tumor chemosensitivity assays on patient-derived tumor cells; the association between PNI status and capecitabine sensitivity was evaluated by ordinal logistic regression with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). Results The six-factor nomogram (T stage, N stage, lymphovascular invasion, tumor budding, KRAS, Ki-67) achieved AUCs of 0.778, 0.741, and 0.803 in the development subset, internal hold-out validation subset and full cohort, respectively, with MAE of 0.023 and Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.56. PNI was independently associated with distant metastasis.Patient-derived tumor cells from PNI-positive tumors exhibited markedly reduced in vitro capecitabine sensitivity, consistent across IPTW (multivariable OR = 0.62, 95% CI 0.44–0.88, P = 0.007) and PSM (multivariable OR = 0.34, 95% CI 0.15–0.77, P = 0.009) analyses. Conclusions PNI-positive CRC harbors a reduced in vitro capecitabine sensitivity and an elevated metastatic propensity. The proposed six-factor nomogram offers a practical postoperative tool for PNI risk stratification, while the convergent clinical and in vitro evidence may inform hypothesis-generating individualized strategies pending prospective validation of fluoropyrimidine-based adjuvant therapy in PNI-positive patients.

papers.abstract: Background Primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma (PPC) is an exceptionally rare and highly aggressive extragonadal trophoblastic malignancy in males, with no established standard treatment. Cytotoxic chemotherapy alone generally yields limited therapeutic benefit, while the role of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains poorly defined. Case presentation Here, we report a 41-year-old man who presented with a six-month history of cough and was found to have a large right upper lobe pulmonary mass with multiple brain metastases. Histopathological examination revealed typical trophoblastic differentiation, and immunohistochemistry demonstrated diffuse positivity for HCG, CK7, GATA3, and SALL4, whereas TTF-1 and Napsin A were negative. Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-HCG) was markedly elevated (> 10, 000 mIU/mL), and no gonadal primary lesion was identified, confirming the diagnosis of primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma. Intervention/outcome The patient underwent multimodal treatment including radiotherapy, EMA/CO chemotherapy, EMA/EP combined with sintilimab, and third-line therapy consisting of nab-paclitaxel, bevacizumab, and penpulimab. Despite intensive treatment, the disease progressed rapidly with new intracranial and systemic metastases. Throughout the disease course, serial β-HCG measurements closely paralleled radiographic findings and provided timely guidance for therapeutic decision-making. In addition, we reviewed previously reported metastatic male PPC cases and performed an exploratory survival analysis, which suggested that patients receiving ICI-based therapy tended to have longer overall survival than those treated without immunotherapy. Conclusion Although these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size, this case highlights the highly aggressive nature of male PPC, emphasizes the diagnostic and monitoring value of dynamic β-HCG assessment, and supports further investigation of chemoimmunotherapy as a potential treatment strategy for this rare malignancy.

papers.abstract: Background Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) is a major etiological factor in gastric carcinogenesis and has been associated with alterations in the tumor immune microenvironment. However, how H. pylori -related transcriptional features intersect with the broader molecular and immune heterogeneity of established gastric cancer remains incompletely characterized. Methods Single-cell RNA-sequencing data (GSE234129) were used for exploratory comparison according to H. pylori status and to define an initial candidate gene set. An eight-gene prognostic signature was subsequently developed in TCGA-STAD and evaluated in independent gastric cancer cohorts. Model-development optimism was assessed using 1, 000 full-pipeline bootstrap resamples. Immune features were evaluated using CIBERSORT, ESTIMATE, TIDE, and immunophenoscore, while observed anti-PD-1 response was explored in the disease-matched PRJEB25780 cohort. RGS1 was further assessed in an independent immunohistochemical cohort. Results Exploratory single-cell analyses suggested differences in immune-cell composition, T-cell states, and antigen-presentation-related pathways according to H. pylori status. The eight-gene prognostic signature stratified overall survival in the TCGA-STAD cohort and two independent GEO cohorts. After full-pipeline bootstrap correction, model discrimination was modest (corrected C-index = 0.575). In TCGA-STAD, addition of the eight-gene score to a clinicopathological model improved prognostic discrimination. High-risk tumors were characterized by distinct stromal, genomic, and immune features, including higher stromal activity, lower tumor mutational burden, and differences in computational immune-response-related profiles. At the tissue level, RGS1 expression was associated with survival and selected immune-cell features. In the IHC cohort, high RGS1 expression remained independently associated with poorer overall survival (OS) after multivariable adjustment (HR = 2.36, 95% CI 1.36-4.10, p = 0.002) and was accompanied by lower CD8-positive and higher CD163-positive and FOXP3-positive cell densities. In the independent H. pylori -annotated GSE62254 cohort, the five non-ribosomal components showed nominal gene-set-level enrichment in H. pylori -positive tumors (CAMERA P = 0.044). Conclusions This study developed an eight-gene survival-associated prognostic signature and characterized its immune associations in gastric cancer. H. pylori -related findings were exploratory and did not establish H. pylori specificity of the final model. Further prospective validation is required given the modest optimism-corrected performance.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by peritoneal dissemination and ascites formation. Kallikrein-related peptidase 5 (KLK5) has been linked to aggressive disease. Building on evidence linking KLK4–7 to keratin 19 (KRT19), we hypothesized that a KLK5–KRT19 axis contributes to tumor progression and investigated this potential axis alongside broader KLK5-associated tumor-cell, metabolic, signaling, and microenvironmental mechanisms. Methods: KLK5-overexpressing ovarian cancer models were characterized using functional assays (adhesion, migration, spheroid formation), KRT19 expression analysis, proteomics, and gene set enrichment analysis. The putative KRT19–KLK5 axis was further investigated in vivo, in silico, and by immunohistochemistry. KLK5-dependent tumor progression was assessed in vivo, including survival and ascites formation, with quantification of CXCL9 in ascitic fluid. Clinical relevance was evaluated by immunohistochemistry in an HGSOC cohort. Results: In vitro, KLK5 overexpression induced KRT19 expression and enhanced spheroid formation, whereas effects on adhesion and migration were limited. Proteomic analysis identified KLK5-associated alterations in cholesterol homeostasis, coagulation, and mTORC1 signaling. In the in vivo mouse model, KLK5 overexpression was associated with reduced survival and increased ascites formation, and KLK5 induced intratumoral KRT19 expression. KLK5 and KRT19 protein levels were positively associated in patient tumors and primary ascites-derived tumor cells. In ascites, KLK5 overexpression was associated with reduced CD3+ cell abundance and lower CXCL9 concentrations. Conclusions: KLK5 promotes HGSOC progression. Its association with KRT19 expression, altered cholesterol homeostasis and mTORC1 signaling, reduced CD3+ cells and CXCL9 in ascites suggests that KLK5 contributes to both tumor-cell and immune features of HGSOC.

papers.abstract: Abstract Chemotherapy is a standard treatment for lung adenocarcinoma, yet the efficacy is often limited, highlighting the need to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of chemoresistance. Given the important role of the tumor microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma progression, we established a biobank of patient-derived lung adenocarcinoma organoids (LCOs) paired with cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) from treatment-naïve tumors and found that coculture with CAFs reduced the drug sensitivity of LCOs. Plasminogen activator urokinase (PLAU) was identified as a specific marker of chemoresistance-associated CAFs linked with poor survival in patients with lung adenocarcinoma. Tumor cells induced polarization of fibroblasts toward a PLAU+ chemoresistant state that secreted C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 5 (CXCL5) to upregulate the endoplasmic reticulum chaperone calmegin (CLGN) in tumor cells. CLGN ablation restored drug sensitivity, whereas CLGN expression was elevated in chemotherapy-resistant lung adenocarcinoma and correlated with pathologic progression. Together, these findings identify the PLAU+ CAF–CXCL5–CLGN axis that drives lung adenocarcinoma chemoresistance and suggest that CLGN inhibition could be a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome chemoresistance in advanced lung adenocarcinoma. Significance: Development of a paired tumor organoid-stroma biobank enabled identification of a PLAU+ fibroblast-CXCL5-CLGN axis that mediates chemoresistance in lung adenocarcinoma, revealing a targetable stromal mechanism with promising therapeutic potential.

papers.abstract: Importance Childhood cancer risk after assisted reproductive technology (ART) remains uncertain, particularly by procedure and cancer type. Objective To examine associations between ART and childhood cancer overall and by ART modality and cancer type. Design, Setting, and Population Nationwide Danish cohort of 1 086 136 live-born children from 1996 to 2012, of whom 37 228 (3.4%) were conceived using ART, with follow-up through 2023. Exposures Maternal ART, classified as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection, or frozen embryo transfer. Main Outcomes and Measures Incident childhood cancer. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); Poisson models estimated incidence rates. Non-ART births were the primary reference; secondary analyses used children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. Results During a median follow-up of 20 years, 3736 cancers occurred. Compared with non-ART births (incidence rate, 18.3 per 100 000 person-years), children conceived using ART had higher cancer incidence (incidence rate, 23.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 1.07-1.48]). Rates were higher after frozen embryo transfer (incidence rate, 41.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.18 [95% CI, 1.45-3.29]) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (incidence rate, 27.9 per 100 000; HR, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.16-1.89]) but not IVF (incidence rate, 18.5 per 100 000; HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.79-1.28]). Frozen embryo transfer was associated with leukemia (incidence rate, 11.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.36 [95% CI, 1.06-5.28]), lymphomas (HR, 3.03 [95% CI, 1.13-8.12]), and soft tissue sarcomas (HR, 7.63 [95% CI, 2.82-20.62]); intracytoplasmic sperm injection was associated with lymphomas (incidence rate, 4.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.94 [95% CI, 1.07-3.54]), soft tissue sarcomas (incidence rate, 3.3 per 100 000; HR, 3.28 [95% CI, 1.54-7.00]), and central nervous system neoplasms (incidence rate, 8.2 per 100 000; HR, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.04-2.57]); no associations were observed for IVF. Findings were similar in secondary analyses using children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. Conclusions and Relevance ART, particularly frozen embryo transfer and intracytoplasmic sperm injection, was associated with increased childhood cancer risk, but absolute risks were low. The consistent results in secondary analyses of children with maternal infertility history or conceived via IVF suggest that procedure-related, rather than infertility-related, factors warrant further investigation.

papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Despite the availability of several approved therapies, continued investigation of novel treatment options is needed to further improve outcomes in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The phase 2 KEYSTEP-004 study evaluated the safety and efficacy of quavonlimab coformulated with pembrolizumab (quavonlimab/pembrolizumab) plus lenvatinib as first-line therapy for advanced HCC. Methods Adults with confirmed advanced HCC and no prior systemic therapy were enrolled. In the safety lead-in phase, participants received intravenous quavonlimab 25 mg coformulated with pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks plus oral lenvatinib 12 mg (body weight ≥60 kg) or 8 mg (body weight <60 kg) once daily (dose level 0 [DL0]). Allocation to the efficacy expansion phase was permitted if lenvatinib DL0 plus quavonlimab 25 mg coformulated with pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks was determined to be tolerable. Primary endpoints were objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 by blinded independent central review (BICR) and safety. Secondary endpoints included duration of response (DOR) and progression-free survival (PFS) per RECIST v1.1 by BICR, and overall survival (OS). Results As of June 22, 2023, 116 participants were enrolled, and 115 were treated. No dose-limiting toxicities were observed in the safety lead-in phase. Lenvatinib DL0 in combination with quavonlimab 25 mg coformulated with pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks was determined to be tolerable. Median study follow-up was 18.0 months (range, 12.0–26.6). Confirmed ORR was 37.4% (95% CI: 28.5–46.9). Median DOR was 10.6 months (range, 1.2+ to 23.1+), median PFS was 8.2 months (95% CI: 6.2–10.2), and median OS was 22.1 months (95% CI: 15.5-not reached). Grade 3–5 treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 66 participants (57.4%); 14 (12.8%) required high-dose steroids for management of a treatment-related AE. Conclusion Quavonlimab coformulated with pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib is an active combination and has a manageable safety profile in advanced HCC.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background The FET-PET in Glioblastoma (FIG) study (TROG 18.06) assessed the impact of adding FET-PET to MRI on radiotherapy gross tumor volume delineation in newly diagnosed glioblastoma. Methods This multicenter prospective phase 2 study evaluated participants with newly diagnosed glioblastoma IDH-wildtype undergoing postoperative MRI and FET-PET imaging before adjuvant radiotherapy, delivered according to standard MRI-based planning. The FET-PET-positive biological tumor volume (BTV) was used to derive the Hybrid (FET-PET+MRI) gross tumor volume (Hybrid-GTV). Primary outcomes were: (1) BTV excluded from the GTV defined on MRI alone (MR-GTV); (2) Hybrid-GTV excluded from the MR-GTV with both comparisons analyzed by non-overlap volume (cm3 and %), dosimetry (D98 and V95), and spatial similarity metrics; (3) clinically meaningful change in GTV non-overlap percentage volume with the addition of FET-PET. Results There were 172 participants recruited, n = 140 evaluable. Median BTV was 23.1 cm3, median MR-GTV was 32.1 cm3, and median Hybrid-GTV was 46.0 cm3. Hybrid-GTV was significantly larger than the MR-GTV (P < .001), with a larger Hybrid-GTV observed in 83% of cases. Comparing BTV to MR-GTV, median non-overlap volume was 10.1 cm3 and non-overlap percentage volume 53.5%. Comparing Hybrid-GTV to MR-GTV, median non-overlap volume was 14.9 cm3 and non-overlap percentage volume 33.9%. D98 and V95 were lower for the Hybrid-GTV than for the MR-GTV, suggesting lower dose coverage. Applying a > 20% non-overlap percentage volume threshold, 76% of participants had a meaningful change in GTV with the addition of FET-PET. Conclusion FET-PET differed significantly from MRI-based GTV delineation, with its incorporation leading to a clinically meaningful change in GTV in the majority of participants.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background H3 K27-altered diffuse midline gliomas (H3-DMGs) are driven by stem-like and proliferative tumor cells resulting from global H3K27me3 loss. Here, we aimed to identify key molecular mechanisms involved in the interplay between epigenetic and epitranscriptomic regulation underlying this process. Methods Patient-derived spinal cord H3-DMG stem-like spheres and serum-induced differentiated cells were used to model tumor plasticity. Multi-omics approaches, including single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, RNA m6A profiling, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and in vitro and in vivo assays were performed to dissect epigenetic and epitranscriptomic regulation of stemness. Results Differentiation reduced stemness markers, proliferation, H3K27M expression, and global m6A levels, while increasing H3K27me3. METTL3 was significantly downregulated during differentiation and positively correlated with stemness and proliferation in patient tumors. METTL3 promoted tumor stemness and growth by stabilizing SOX11 mRNA through YTHDC2-dependent m6A recognition. In parallel, H3K27me3 loss relieved transcriptional repression at both METTL3 and SOX11 loci, leading to SOX11 overexpression. Functionally, SOX11 interacted with SMARCA4, the core ATPase of the SWI/SNF complex, to enhance chromatin accessibility and activate stemness-associated transcriptional programs marked by H3K27ac and H3K4me3 enrichment. Clinically, METTL3 and SOX11 were upregulated in H3K27M-mutant tumors, and high SOX11 expression correlated with increased proliferation, poor prognosis, and enhanced sensitivity to the SMARCA4 inhibitor BRM014. Conclusions H3K27M-driven epigenetic dysregulation promotes SOX11 overexpression through combined H3K27me3 loss and METTL3-mediated m6A modification. SOX11 sustains tumor stemness and proliferation by recruiting SMARCA4 to remodel chromatin and serves as both a prognostic biomarker and a predictor of response to SMARCA4-targeted therapy in spinal cord H3-DMG.

papers.abstract: Abstract PURPOSE To examine whether Medicare’s 2018 National Coverage Determination (NCD) for next-generation sequencing (NGS) was associated with changes in the use of targeted oral anticancer therapies among older adults with lung cancer. METHODS Retrospective cohort study. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate the probability of initiating an oral targeted therapy within 12 months of diagnosis. Key exposures were (1) diagnosis before versus after the NCD and (2) residence in a region with versus without pre-NCD NGS. Data were drawn from the SEER–Medicare linked data with Part D claims, including diagnosis years 2016–2019 with follow-up through 2020. The analytic sample included Medicare fee-for-service Part D beneficiaries aged 65 years or older with newly diagnosed lung cancer. RESULTS Among 30,855 Medicare fee-for-service Part D beneficiaries with lung cancer, 7.1% used targeted oral anticancer therapies. The NCD was not associated with a significant overall change in targeted therapy use (0.4 Percentage Point; 95% CI, −1.6 to 2.4; p = 0.71). Before NCD implementation, targeted therapy use was 1.0 PP higher in regions with pre-NCD NGS coverage than in regions without such coverage (95% CI, 0.2–1.9; p = 0.015). In stage-stratified analyses, the additional post-NCD change was significant among patients with distant-stage disease (3.2 PPs; 95% CI, 2.6–4.0; p < 0.001) but not among those with regional-stage disease (p = 0.29). CONCLUSIONS Medicare's NCD for NGS was not associated with a significant overall increase in targeted oral anticancer therapy use but was associated with increased use among patients with distant-stage disease. Targeted therapy use remained higher in regions with preexisting NGS coverage.

papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction We sought to evaluate the associations of post-diagnostic consumption of flavonoids and flavonoid-rich foods with survival among patients with stage III colon cancer enrolled in a clinical trial. Methods We conducted a prospective observational study of 1625 patients with stage III colon cancer enrolled in the CALGB/SWOG 80702 (Alliance) randomized adjuvant chemotherapy trial who completed a self-reported food frequency questionnaire within 6 weeks of and again 14-16 months post-randomization. Intakes of flavonoids overall and by subclasses (anthocyanidins, flavanones, flavan-3-ols, flavones, flavonols, isoflavones) were computed by multiplying the consumption frequency of each dietary item by the nutrient content of its respective specified portions. Multivariable analyses for the primary (disease-free survival [DFS]) and secondary (overall survival [OS]) endpoints were adjusted for sociodemographic, clinical, dietary, and lifestyle factors. Bonferroni corrections were applied for analyses of flavonoid subclasses and flavonoid-rich foods. Results Over median follow-up of 5.9 years, flavonoid consumption either overall or by subclasses was not significantly associated with survival outcomes, with a hazard ratio (HR) (95% confidence interval [CI]) of 1.01 (0.75-1.37) for DFS among those in the highest relative to lowest consumption quintiles of total flavonoids. Exploratory analyses of flavonoid-rich foods intake did not demonstrate significant associations with DFS or OS after Bonferroni correction. Conclusion Among resected stage III colon cancer patients who received standardized treatment and follow-up within a nationwide randomized clinical trial, consumption of flavonoids was not associated with survival outcomes. papers.abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and BRAF/MEK kinase inhibitors have substantially improved survival in advanced melanoma; however, therapeutic resistance and severe toxicities underscore the ongoing need for alternative strategies. Here, we evaluate the clinical utility of multi-omic profiling, biomarker-stratified recommendations, and survival outcomes within a prospective cohort of 98 patients with advanced cutaneous or uveal melanoma evaluated by the Molecular Tumor Board Freiburg (MTB-FR) between 2021 and 2024. Completed profiling revealed at least one potential actionable target beyond classical BRAF V600 mutations in 83.8% of cases. Alterations in NRAS , atypical BRAF variants, CDK4/6 pathway amplifications, and DNA-damage response (DDR) gene mutations most frequently guided board recommendations. Biomarker-stratified therapies were recommended for 68.4% of patients, and personalized immunotherapy combinations for 72.4%. The treatment implementation rate was 33.8% (n = 27), achieving an overall disease control rate (DCR) of 42.9% and an overall response rate (ORR) of 10.7%. These findings demonstrate that comprehensive molecular profiling in a real-world setting uncovers actionable alterations, providing viable subsequent treatment avenues that may optimize outcomes for heavily pretreated melanoma patients beyond established standards of care. Ultimately, prospective, randomized, biomarker-driven trials remain essential to validate whether these individualized diagnostic strategies translate into a reproducible survival benefit.

papers.abstract: Rhythmic gene expression is controlled by oscillating recruitment of specific transcription factors and co-regulators, including histone-modifying enzymes and chromatin-remodeling complexes. To unravel the significance of SWI/SNF ATPase subunits in diurnal chromatin remodeling, we have mapped diurnal chromatin accessibility, SWI/SNF occupancy, and gene expression throughout a day in the liver of male mice exposed to a night restricted feeding regimen. We find remarkable remodeling during fasting-to-fed transitions, and a third of rhythmic enhancers exhibited diurnal SWI/SNF occupancy and accessibility. Hepatocyte-specific disruption of either of the two mutually exclusive ATPases of SWI/SNF has minor effects on chromatin accessibility. However, simultaneous disruption of both ATPases results in a collapse of chromatin accessibility in the majority of distal cis-regulatory and a third of promoter proximal cis-regulatory elements, which leads to disrupted diurnal gene expression and signs of liver damage and inflammation. SWI/SNF-dependent promoters exhibit similarities with diurnal promoters, indicating a potential sequence-level bias that favors dynamic SWI/SNF-mediated chromatin remodeling. Collectively, this suggests an essential role of SWI/SNF-mediated chromatin remodeling of cis-regulatory regions for rhythmic gene expression and basic liver function.

papers.abstract: The realization of efficient 1.54 µm electroluminescence from erbium ions is persistently hampered by their intrinsically small absorption cross-section and low excitation efficiency in conventional hosts. This study addresses this by synthesizing lead-free Cs3CrBr6 perovskite nanocrystals. This material is a direct-bandgap n-type chromium-based halide semiconductor whose electronic structure provides good charge transport, serving as a suitable host for lanthanide doping. Er3+ incorporation serves as an efficient luminescent center and modulates the host's band structure. Leveraging the broadband absorption of Cr3+ for sensitization, combined with surface passivation, we achieve highly efficient Cr3+ to Er3+ energy transfer. This yields intense 1.54 µm emission with a photoluminescence quantum yield of 47%. The corresponding electroluminescent device attains a peak external quantum efficiency of 3.26%, among the highest values reported for solution-processed, Er3+-based near-infrared light-emitting diodes. This performance robustly validates the host's effectiveness in facilitating charge injection and transport. Consequently, this work provides a viable material strategy for high-performance 1.54 µm emission and lays a solid foundation for chromium-based halide perovskites in advanced optoelectronics.

papers.abstract: Optical fibers are widely used to transmit optical signals for communications and sensing. Extending this capability to hyperspectral imaging is attractive for compact imaging systems, but is fundamentally constrained by limited channel capacity and transmission distortion of fibers. Here, we demonstrate single-fiber hyperspectral imaging via nanophotonic disordered dispersion. A disordered-dispersion encoder at the distal fiber end can map high-dimensional spectral-angular information into a one-dimensional spectral measurement, which is then computationally decoded using sparsity-constrained reconstruction. Our disordered dispersion is achieved using nonlocal nanophotonic structures that support high mode density and multimode coupling, thereby enabling low-correlation compressive encoding. The system features angular reconstruction over a field of view of ±60°, spectral detection from 400 to 700 nm, and robustness against fiber distortion. This work circumvents the need for real-space pixelated encoders or detectors used in traditional hyperspectral cameras, offering a route toward ultra-compact high-dimensional imagers compatible with flexible single-fiber probes.

papers.abstract: Kagome lattices host exotic phenomena such as quantum spin liquids, topological Weyl nodes, and flat bands. The kagome ferromagnet Co3Sn2S2 has been a focus of debate due to conflicting reports on its magnetic character. Here, using weakly perturbative probes-primarily neutron scattering and Mössbauer spectroscopy-we determine its ground state and magnetic Hamiltonian. The spin wave spectrum is reproduced by a simple Hamiltonian dominated by a large in-plane nearest-neighbor Heisenberg interaction J and an antisymmetric Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction that is roughly one third of J. This Hamiltonian yields a canted, noncollinear ferromagnetic ground state with an umbrella-type structure, which our data show to be the true ground state at all temperatures below TC. Additionally, the spin susceptibility above TC exhibits a reduced critical exponent, akin to other spin-anisotropic systems. Our findings explain the unconventional magnetism in Co3Sn2S2, including the giant anomalous Hall effect and the origin of chiral phonons.

papers.abstract: DNA methyltransferase DNMT1 plays an essential role in maintaining DNA methylation homeostasis. While DNMT1-mediated DNA methylation mainly occurs outside the active chromatin domains, such as CpG islands, how DNMT1 interplays with hypomethylated nucleosome environment to restrict CpG island methylation remains unclear. Here we report the structure of DNMT1 with a nucleosome containing unmodified CpG sites. The interaction of the DNMT1 CXXC domain with the unmodified CpG sites within the nucleosome core or the linker strengthens the DNMT1-nucleosome association, which contributes to the enrichment of DNMT1 in CpG islands. On the other hand, the CXXC domain is positioned in a manner that blocks the target recognition domain of DNMT1 from accessing potential DNA substrates. Consistently, disrupting the CXXC-CpG interaction leads to DNMT1 hyperactivity on nucleosomes with unmodified CpG sites, or those with spatially proximate unmodified and hemimethylated CpG sites. Furthermore, our whole-genome bisulfite-sequencing analysis reveals that introducing the CXXC-CpG interaction-defective DNMT1 mutation leads to substantial increase in CpG island methylation but not so much in overall genomic methylation, causing severe defects in transcriptional programming and stem cell differentiation. Together, this study establishes a role for the CXXC domain in safeguarding the CpG island hypomethylation, vital to DNA methylation homeostasis during development.

papers.abstract: Human prions and amyloids exhibit structural diversity that correlates with different pathological manifestations. Yeast prions represent a convenient model for studying fundamental properties of prions and their strain diversity. The Sup35 yeast prion has multiple structural variants, divided into "strong" and "weak" groups differing in frequency of fibril fragmentation and resulting nonsense-suppression. The molecular origin of these distinctions remains unclear. Here, we show that the different frequency of prion fragmentation is determined by their stability, rather than the efficiency of chaperone binding. The fully protease-resistant part (residues 2-32) of the Sup35 prion core is a key for the prion phenotype and maintenance, whereas partially resistant part (33-72) is less important. We established the cryo-EM structure of a strong Sup35 prion variant purified from yeast, comprising residues 2-64, with 2.7 Å resolution. Comparison of this structure with that of Sup35 amyloid formed in vitro at 4˚C revealed their significant difference.

papers.abstract: Real-time monitoring of safety-critical interior states remains an open problem across energy, environmental, and industrial systems where direct instrumentation is infeasible. Existing approaches based on governing equations, discrete state vectors, or fixed sensor locations fail to provide mesh-independent, field-level reconstructions at arbitrary interior coordinates under real-time constraints. Here we introduce neural operator-based virtual sensing as a general framework for recovering inaccessible interior fields from sparse, heterogeneous measurements and operating conditions, instantiated with MIMONet, a multi-input, multi-output neural operator that fuses heterogeneous inputs and decodes coupled physical fields through a shared latent representation. Across three engineering-grade evaluations of escalating complexity, from confined recirculating flows to pressurized water reactor subchannels and compact power-system heat exchangers, MIMONet achieves ≤5% relative reconstruction error, while generating full-field predictions with sub-millisecond inference on an NVIDIA H200, at least five orders of magnitude faster than traditional high-fidelity CFD simulations, with calibrated uncertainty and noise resilience demonstrated on the heat-exchanger case. We validate the framework on three independent real-world datasets spanning electrochemical energy, atmospheric science, and physical oceanography: current-density mapping in a hydrogen fuel cell, wind-speed profiling on instrumented meteorological towers, and North Atlantic ocean-state from a global ocean reanalysis. MIMONet improves over classical virtual-sensing baselines by 72-84%: 84% on fuel-cell internal-field recovery from 10% sensor coverage and 83% on hub-height wind-speed recovery from lower-level tower sensors. Most notably, it recovers sea-surface height, a field with zero direct sensors, from its learned coupling to observed temperature and salinity at 4.1 × lower error than the best classical predictor, a cross-modal field recovery beyond the reach of classical interpolation. These results establish operator-based virtual sensing as a practical route to real-time field observability in systems where the states that matter most cannot be directly measured.

papers.abstract: Molecular prediction depends on how chemical structures are represented, yet descriptors capture only partial aspects of chemical information. Here, we show that the Chemical Dice Integrator combines six complementary molecular views spanning physicochemical properties, molecular topology, two-dimensional structural images, bioactivity profiles, quantum properties, and molecular language into a unified latent space. This multimodal representation is distilled into a sequence-based model that generates the embedding directly from molecular strings. Across classification and regression benchmarks, the representation outperformed classical fusion methods, matched or improved established molecular descriptors, retained complete embedding coverage when individual feature-generation pipelines failed, and supported efficient inference. Scaffold-based and low-data evaluations showed stable generalization across chemical space and improved utility under limited data. The framework also prioritized compounds predicted to protect genome stability, leading to experimental validation of isoeugenol and eugenyl acetate in a yeast damage-response assay. These findings establish a scalable framework for molecular prediction and discovery.

papers.abstract: Arthropod-borne, positive-sense RNA viruses encompass many human pathogens posing significant health threats worldwide. Understanding intracellular dynamics and host-factor interactions of the viral genome is essential for devising effective antiviral strategies. Here, we engineer dual-labeled Zika and chikungunya viruses incorporating a Mango-II aptamer for RNA pulldown and real-time imaging, achieving high-resolution imaging of flavivirus RNA in live cells. Tandem imaging with viral replication proteins revealed intracellular dynamics of replication complexes and RNA molecules of these viruses. We identify >200 high-confidence host interactors of viral RNA and corroborated 355 hits from existing data sets. Spliceosome factor SFPQ is as a common interactor decreasing RNA production in both viruses when depleted. Intracellular colocalization of SFPQ-ZIKV and SFPQ-CHIKV RNA is confirmed through confocal microscopy imaging of infected cells. Thus, we demonstrate Mango-II aptamer tagging as an innovative strategy for identifying spatiotemporal dynamics and virus-host interactions of viral genomes in positive-strand RNA viruses.

papers.abstract: Cell surface proteins represent an important source of biomarkers and therapeutic targets. However, due to the inherent sensitivity limitations of existing technologies, tissue and cell-type-specific surfaceomes remain poorly characterized, especially in the context of human diseases. Here, we present nanoMAPS (nanoscale Magnetic Affinity Purification System), a miniaturized proteomic sample preparation method for surfaceome profiling of as few as 100-500 cells (~100,000-fold lower than existing technologies). By performing magnetic bead-based affinity purification within a single microliter-scale droplet, nanoMAPS significantly improves the recovery of surface proteins and reduces non-specific absorption of intracellular proteins. Application of nanoMAPS to primary human immune cells and mouse plasma cell populations enables robust identification of established cell-type-specific surface markers as well as other proteins selectively enriched in disease-associated immune cell subpopulations. Together, these results establish nanoMAPS as a broadly applicable platform for extending surface proteomics technology to rare primary cells isolated directly from diseased tissues.

papers.abstract: Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) are typically estimated to have lower attributional lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions than conventional internal combustion engine vehicles. These estimates rely upon lower usage emissions outweighing higher manufacturing emissions, but limited data on electric vehicle mileage, and how long they last, casts uncertainty over comparisons. Here we use data for every electric vehicle in Britain to assess mileage and lifetime compared to conventional and hybrid vehicles, and the implications for attributional lifecycle emissions. We find that first-generation BEVs were driven less and have not lasted as long as conventional vehicles, yet still had lower lifecycle emissions. The annual mileage and lifetime of BEVs purchased in 2026 will equal conventional vehicles if recent trends continue. Training a transformer neural network on this data, we estimate that current BEVs have projected attributional lifecycle emissions of 88 g CO2e per kilometre, less than half the 254-270 g for conventional vehicles and 190 g for hybrid vehicles, based on real-world usage.

papers.abstract: Optical beam steering is a key technology for free-space optical communication, sensing, and imaging. Mechanical beam steering systems suffer from limited scanning speed and bulky form factors, while existing solid-state solutions rely on pixelated synthetic aperture that requires complex fabrication and control architectures. Integrated acousto-optic beam steering is an emerging technology that enables continuous one-dimensional beam steering using integrated acoustic transducers and fixed-wavelength laser sources. Here, we integrate this approach with an optical ring resonator on the same thin-film lithium niobate platform to significantly enhance beam steering efficiency and system functionality. The resulting device achieves a resonance-enhanced beam steering efficiency of up to 26% and a field of view of 18∘. Moreover, by leveraging integrated electro-optic control, we dynamically lock the ring-resonator's resonance to a chirped laser frequency, enabling frequency-modulated continuous-wave light detection and ranging operation. By combining lithium niobate's piezoelectric and electro-optic properties, this work establishes a compact, efficient, and scalable beam-steering platform with co-integrated acousto-optic modulation and electro-optic control for multifunctional applications.

papers.abstract: To maximize their reproductive success, nematodes not only must arrest their development in response to adverse growth conditions but also must quickly recover if conditions improve. However, the molecular signals that coordinate these transitions remain poorly understood. Here, we show that a hybrid polyketide synthase (PKS)-nonribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) expressed in the canal-associated neurons (CANs) is a central regulator of multiple developmental arrest programs, including starvation-induced larval arrest and dauer development. Using unbiased, comparative metabolomics in the predatory nematode Pristionchus pacificus, we show that this PKS-NRPS assembly line produces a suite of secondary metabolites, including a family of hybrid polyketide-nonribosomal peptides known as the nemamides, the related nemaketides, and a family of ascarylose-modified polyketides that we term ascarenes. Depending on the starter unit that is loaded onto the assembly line, the PKS-NRPS megasynthetase can produce dramatically different downstream products. Genetic analysis of the assembly line suggests that the nemamides promote recovery from starvation-induced larval arrest, while the ascarenes inhibit dauer development. Our work demonstrates that the PKS-NRPS assembly line serves as a signaling hub in the CANs, producing multiple signaling molecules that control different developmental events.

papers.abstract: Photonic crystals are typically fabricated with a fixed topology, freezing their edge and corner states in space and frequency. Here we introduce a kirigami-actuated reconfigurable topological photonic crystal in which a single in-plane rotation reshapes the unit cell, drives a bandgap closure and reopening, and thereby relocates the Wannier center and switches the associated Zak phase-the topological invariant that determines whether boundary states appear. We engineer a symmetry-preserving square-lattice deformation path that programs the intracell rod configuration into a compact, discrete topological phase library. Using this library, we demonstrate reconfigurable control of topological modes in both resonance frequency and spatial localization from the same mechanical degree of freedom. A higher-order corner mode is switched between two distinct resonance frequencies while its localization moves between different geometric corners. Meanwhile, at a fixed operating frequency, the propagation path of reciprocal crystalline-symmetry-protected edge modes is mechanically rewritten, enabling on/off gating and two-path beam routing. These results establish a route toward reconfigurable topological photonic devices, showing that quantized band topology can be encoded and switched by shape.

papers.abstract: Curved and conformal optics provide additional geometric degrees of freedom that enable enhanced optical performance while satisfying non-optical constraints such as ergonomics, aerodynamics, and wearability. However, existing fabrication approaches for curved metasurfaces are limited in scalability, geometry control, and alignment accuracy. Here we show a scalable fabrication strategy for curved and conformal metasurface optics based on thermoforming, an industry-standard manufacturing process for thermoplastics. Our approach enables wafer-scale production of highly curved metasurfaces with millimeter-level radii of curvature and micron-level alignment precision. We develop a predictive thermorheological model that accurately captures and compensates for the large deformations induced during thermoforming, preserving the intended optical response and enabling diffraction-limited performance. As demonstrations, we realize freestanding curved metalenses, conformal refractive-metasurface hybrid optics, and an artificial compound eye with a wide field of view, reduced aberrations, and uniform imaging performance. These results establish thermoforming as a scalable manufacturing platform for next-generation conformal photonic systems.

papers.abstract: Epidemiological studies link kidney function to Parkinson's disease risk, but the genetic basis of this relationship remains unclear. Here, we leverage genome-wide association data for Parkinson's disease and five UK Biobank-derived kidney-related traits in individuals of European ancestry, combining genetic correlation, pleiotropy mapping, colocalization and enrichment across sex-combined and sex-stratified analyses. Genome-wide genetic correlations with Parkinson's are modest, with only a significant correlation with urinary potassium-to-creatinine ratio significant, yet we identify shared loci across 9 of 15 trait pairs. Resolving these loci, the two traits are more often driven by different causal variants within a shared region than by the same variant. Four loci carry a shared causal variant, implicating BIN3, MSRA and TNK2 in protein quality control. These findings provide evidence for shared genomic loci between Parkinson's disease and kidney function, offering specific loci and biological pathways for future investigation of the kidney-brain axis in neurodegeneration.

papers.abstract: Histone H3 lysine 36 dimethylation (H3K36me2) plays a key role in transcriptional elongation and chromatin organization, yet how its deposition is spatially controlled across the genome remains unclear. Here, we identify TOP1 as a critical recruiter of the H3K36me2 methyltransferase NSD2 to gene bodies. Disruption of the TOP1-NSD2 interaction reduces H3K36me2 at gene bodies, impairs RNA polymerase II release, and represses transcription. Remarkably, loss of this recruitment increases H3K36me2 at repetitive sequences, licensing their aberrant transcriptional activation. We show that NSD2 is primarily responsible for depositing H3K36me2 at these loci. We further identify MTA1 as a recruiter of NSD2 to repetitive elements via recognition of the GATC consensus sequence. Together, TOP1 and MTA1 spatially partition NSD2 across the genome, enabling H3K36me2 to serve dual roles in regulating canonical gene expression and acting as an active mark for the transcriptional activation of repetitive sequences.

papers.abstract: Multimodal locomotion is crucial for an animal's adaptability in unstructured wild environments. Analogously, in the human gastrointestinal tract, characterized by viscoelastic mucus, complex rugae, and narrow openings like the cardia, multimodal locomotion is also essential for a small-scale soft robot to conduct tasks. Here, we introduce a small-scale, compact, foldable, and robust soft electromagnetic robot with more than nine locomotion modes designed for such a scenario. Featuring a six-spoke elastomer body embedded with liquid metal channels and driven by Laplace forces under a static magnetic field, the robot is capable of rapid transitions ( < 0.35 s) among different locomotion modes. It achieves exceptional agility, including high-speed rolling (818 mm/s, 26 body lengths per second), omnidirectional crawling, jumping, and swimming. Notably, the robot can fold to reduce its occupied volume by 79%, enabling it to traverse confined spaces. We further validate its navigation capabilities in unstructured environments, including discrete obstacles, viscoelastic gelatin surfaces, viscous fluids, 3D-printed gastric surfaces, and a porcine gastric environment. This system offers a versatile strategy for developing high-mobility soft robots for future biomedical applications.

papers.abstract: Lytic bacteriophages, viruses that lyse (kill) bacteria, hold great promise for treating infections, including wound infections caused by antimicrobial-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. However, dosing and delivery strategies for phage therapy remain underdeveloped. In a mouse wound infection model specifically designed to evaluate the treatment of established infections-a critical gap in existing preclinical models-we investigated the impact of administration route, dose, and frequency on phage therapy efficacy. In this model, topical, but not systemic, delivery reduced wound bacterial burden. In vitro and in vivo data revealed rapid emergence of phage resistance and suggested potential benefit of using high and repeated doses. Building on these insights, we developed HydroPhage, a phage-containing hyaluronan-based hydrogel formed with dynamic covalent crosslinks that delivers high-titer phages over one week. Here, we show that sustained hydrogel-based delivery is a practical and effective approach for topical phage application.

papers.abstract: This phase 3 multicenter trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of adding dual epigenetic agents azacitidine and chidamide to CHOP (AC-CHOP) versus CHOP alone in previously untreated peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). A total of 128 patients were enrolled from 9 centers in China and assigned according to participating centers (AC-CHOP, N = 84; CHOP, N = 44). Azacitidine 200 mg on days 1-2, 100 mg on day 3 and chidamide 20 mg twice weekly were administered in the AC-CHOP arm. The AC-CHOP arm showed numerically higher ORR (60.7% vs. 54.6%) and CR rate (47.6% vs. 36.4%) than the CHOP arm, although the differences were not statistically significant. A trend toward improved PFS was observed in the AC-CHOP arm (median 10.2 months in the AC-CHOP arm vs. 8.4 months in the CHOP arm, P = 0.093), alongside a significantly improved OS (median 46.2 months vs. 24.1 months, P = 0.023). The safety profile was comparable between the two groups, with hematologic toxicity and infection being the most common adverse events. Genomic profiling showed that DNMT3A mutations were associated with lower response rates, while IDH2 and TP53 mutations were associated with inferior survival outcomes. In conclusion, the addition of chidamide and azacitidine to CHOP did not significantly improve ORR or PFS. Although OS was longer in the AC-CHOP arm, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the imbalances in post-protocol treatments between the two arms. Integration of molecular profiling may improve risk stratification and inform future biomarker-driven therapeutic strategies in PTCL.
