papers.abstract: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an established biomarker for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, it remains unclear whether biomarkers reflecting amyloid-β metabolism (Aβ), tau (phosphorylated tau, pTau), and astrogliosis (glial fibrillary acidic protein, GFAP) can complement NfL in clinical applications. It is also unclear how Alzheimer's disease (AD) co-pathology affects disease progression in ALS. We studied 264 patients with ALS and 164 disease-control participants, analysing baseline cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) NfL, Aβ peptides, pTau181, pTau217, and GFAP. A two-step diagnostic strategy was examined in individuals with intermediate NfL values, using machine-learning models. Prognostic associations were evaluated using linear mixed-effects and Cox models adjusted for established predictors; survival was additionally examined in pooled analyses including an external ALS cohort (n = 153). Patients with ALS exhibited higher CSF NfL, Aβ38, Aβ40, Aβ42, pTau181, and pTau217 than controls, even within Aβ-negative subgroups. NfL discriminated ALS from controls with an AUC of 0.85 (0.82-0.88), which increased to 0.90 (0.88-0.92) in machine-learning models incorporating additional biomarkers. The machine-learning models maintained a high positive predictive value (0.90) for classifying cases with intermediate NfL values. Significant Aβ × NfL interactions were observed for longitudinal functional decline, and pooled survival analyses showed stronger associations between NfL and survival in the Aβ-positive ALS subgroup (14%) than in the Aβ-negative ALS subgroup (HR 4.02 [2.17-7.45] vs 1.62 [1.36-1.92]). Multiple biomarker assessments can reduce misclassification of individuals with intermediate NfL values. CSF Aβ positivity modified the association between baseline NfL and disease progression. Personalised diagnosis and prognosis based on fine-grained co-pathology evaluation may enhance clinical management of ALS. This study was primarily supported by JST SPRING (JPMJSP2125). papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) are produced in enteroendocrine L cells and control energy homeostasis. GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) activation improves glucose homeostasis and induces satiety and weight loss, whereas GLP-2 receptor (GLP-2R) signaling promotes intestinal growth and nutrient absorption. GLP-1R and GLP-2R agonism also reduce intestinal damage in preclinical studies. Here, we demonstrate that endogenous GLP-1R and GLP-2R signaling are essential for protecting the intestine from T cell-mediated enteropathy. Gut injury induced by T cell activation is increased in Glp1r-/- and Glp2r-/- mice, as well as in mice with selective loss of intestinal proglucagon gene expression (GcgGut-/-). Conversely, the GLP-2R agonist teduglutide and the GLP-1R agonist semaglutide, administered separately or together, attenuate αCD3-induced intestinal damage in GcgGut-/- mice. Collectively, these findings demonstrate distinct biological roles for endogenous GLP-1R/GLP-2R activity in immune-mediated intestinal injury and highlight the therapeutic potential of glucagon-like peptides, alone or together, for ameliorating T cell-mediated mucosal injury.

papers.abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of Crohn's disease, for which targeted therapies remain unavailable. Fibrosis is defined by excess matrix deposition, which may result from inadequate phagocytic clearance, yet how phagocytosis shifts here is unclear. Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, we identify fibrosis-associated CD47hi fibroblasts coupled to SIRPAhi macrophages in fibrotic regions. Cell-cell communication analyses and neutralizing-antibody experiments identify interleukin-1β as a mediator of their crosstalk, forming a profibrotic niche characterized by phagocytic evasion. Genetic disruption of fibroblast Cd47 or macrophage Sirpa enhances fibroblast clearance and attenuates fibrosis. Mechanistically, checkpoint disruption reprograms macrophages toward an NRF2-associated pro-phagocytic state, linking enhanced clearance to the antifibrotic response. Furthermore, therapeutic antibody blockade of this checkpoint attenuates intestinal fibrosis in mouse models with schedule-dependent efficacy. Collectively, these findings support CD47-mediated phagocytic evasion as a key pathogenic mechanism in intestinal fibrosis and identify CD47-SIRPα blockade as a promising therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Clinical T1 micropapillary urothelial carcinoma of the bladder is an aggressive variant histology for which early radical cystectomy (RC) is commonly recommended. However, there remain conflicting data on whether conditions in carefully selected patients may be managed with initial bladder-sparing approaches without compromising oncologic outcomes. The objective is to systematically review and synthesize the available literature comparing bladder-sparing approaches, such as Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) therapy, and early RC outcomes in clinical stage 1 primary tumor (cT1) micropapillary carcinoma of the bladder. A systematic search was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement and Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions. The primary end points were overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS). The included articles were descriptively assessed and time-to-event analysis was performed for select endpoints. Among 461 identified reports, nine retrospective studies met the criteria for quantitative analysis, encompassing 9402 patients of whom 9287 (99%) had non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) and 1033 (11%) had a micropapillary subtype. A total of 625 patients (62%) underwent bladder-sparing approaches, whereas 392 (39%) underwent early RC. Of the bladder-sparing approaches, 88% of patients received intravesical BCG therapy. For a bladder-sparing approach for cT1 disease with a micropapillary component, pooled unadjusted hazard ratios were not statistically significant for CSS (hazard ratio [HR] 1.32, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.60-2.88, p = 0.5) and OS (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.68-1.07, p = 0.16) compared with early RC. Data evaluating bladder-sparing strategies beyond BCG were limited. NMIBC with micropapillary features is an aggressive disease conventionally managed with early RC. In retrospective cohorts of selected patients with micropapillary cT1, available unadjusted data did not provide clear evidence of statistically significant differences in CSS or OS between initial bladder-sparing approaches and early RC.

papers.abstract: Background: Accurate pretreatment prediction of pCR is critical for stratifying patients with LARC and selecting candidates for organ-preserving approaches. However, pCR is a postoperative pathological endpoint, whereas watch-and-wait strategies are based on cCR. Despite a rapidly expanding literature encompassing gene expression signatures, MRI radiomics, deep learning, and multi-modal fusion models, no prior systematic review has comprehensively evaluated predictive performance across all modalities using contemporary meta-analytic techniques for diagnostic test accuracy. Methods: Systematic review and random- effects meta-analysis of studies developing or validating predictive models for pCR in LARC treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) were conducted. Summary AUC was estimated using logit-transformed random-effects models. Heterogeneity was quantified by I2 and τ2. Subgroup analyses were performed according to model modality and validation strategy. Publication bias was assessed with Egger’s linear regression test. Sensitivity analyses were performed using leave-one-out cross-validation. Results: Forty-three studies with 67,302 patients were included. The pooled AUC across all models was 0.874 (95% CI: 0.855–0.892), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 94.3%, τ2 = 0.247). Deep learning models showed the highest pooled AUC (0.919, 95% CI: 0.877–0.948), with MRI radiomics (0.885, 95% CI: 0.852–0.911), multi-modal (0.875, 95% CI: 0.813–0.919), gene expression (0.855, 95% CI: 0.797–0.898), and clinical factors (0.820, 95% CI: 0.788–0.849) showing progressively lower pooled estimates. External validation cohorts had a lower pooled AUC (0.864) than internal validation (0.884). Significant publication bias was detected (Egger’s test p < 0.001). Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis confirmed robustness of the overall estimate. Conclusions: Deep learning and MRI radiomics models demonstrate promising diagnostic accuracy for predicting pCR after nCRT in LARC. However, the predominance of retrospective, single-center designs with limited external validation represents a critical translational gap, and the lack of studies in the total neoadjuvant therapy era limits generalizability. Prospective, multicenter validation studies incorporating standardized endpoints and class imbalance-appropriate metrics are urgently needed.

papers.abstract: Background Muscle strength and muscle mass may decline discordantly in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but the prognostic relevance of combined strength–mass phenotypes during hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC)-based combination therapy is unclear. We evaluated survival and incremental prognostic value according to handgrip strength (HGS) and skeletal muscle index (SMI) phenotypes in patients with unresectable HCC. Methods We performed a secondary analysis of 154 patients from the 1:1 propensity score-matched subset of a previously reported 265-patient cohort receiving HAIC with targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Patients were classified as Normal, SMI-low, HGS-low, or Both-low. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were assessed using Kaplan–Meier and multivariable Cox analyses. Incremental prognostic value for OS was evaluated using Harrell’s concordance index (C-index) and likelihood-ratio tests, with internal validation using bootstrap optimism correction. Results Median follow-up was 22.1 months, as estimated using the reverse Kaplan–Meier method. PFS and OS differed across phenotypes (both log-rank P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, HGS-low was associated with shorter PFS (hazard ratio [HR], 2.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.71–4.60) and OS (HR, 3.09; 95% CI, 1.87–5.11), and Both-low showed similar associations (PFS: HR, 2.53; 95% CI, 1.40–4.56; OS: HR, 3.72; 95% CI, 2.00–6.92). The 10-patient SMI-low estimates were imprecise for PFS (HR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.29–2.16) and OS (HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.28–2.31). After bootstrap optimism correction, adding low HGS increased the C-index from 0.625 to 0.705, whereas the four-phenotype model yielded 0.701 and did not improve model fit beyond low HGS ( P = 0.798). Conclusion Low HGS, with or without low SMI, was associated with poorer survival. HGS may provide a simple and practical measure for baseline prognostic assessment in unresectable HCC treated with HAIC-based combination therapy.

papers.abstract: Hepatic portal venous gas (HPVG) is an uncommon radiological sign whose clinical importance depends on the underlying disorder and the patient’s physiological state. Only two cases of HPVG following transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) have been reported. We describe a rapidly fatal episode in a 71-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B and biopsy-confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma. Selective TACE involved lobaplatin infusion, followed by 10 mL of an iodized oil-raltitrexed emulsion and 1 mL of epirubicin-loaded drug-eluting microspheres. Constipation and abdominal distension developed approximately 21 h after TACE. Severe abdominal pain and vomiting followed at 37 h. Emergency CT at approximately 38 h showed peripheral branching HPVG, bowel dilatation, and intraluminal fluid. At approximately 39 h, the patient developed impaired consciousness, hypotension, and bradycardia. He died despite resuscitative treatment approximately 40 h after TACE. Lactate, a repeat leukocyte count, blood cultures, and other microbiological samples were not obtained after the acute deterioration. Sepsis therefore remained an unconfirmed possible mechanism. The combined embolization regimen represents a procedural exposure, not a proven cause. Progressive abdominal symptoms after TACE should prompt urgent evaluation for bowel injury, infection, biliary complications, and circulatory deterioration.

papers.abstract: Introduction Bilateral vestibulopathy (BVP) presents with oscillopsia, unsteadiness, and imbalance. Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a rare and underrecognized cause of BVP, with direct infiltration of the vestibulocochlear nerves representing a potential mechanism of bilateral vestibular dysfunction. We report a case of LM-related BVP documented by quantitative video head impulse test (vHIT) of all six semicircular canals. Case report A 61-year-old man presented with a six-month history of dizziness, tinnitus, oscillopsia, imbalance, and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. vHIT showed reduced vestibulo-ocular reflex gain in all six semicircular canals. Contrast-enhanced MRI revealed leptomeningeal enhancement and enhancement of both vestibulocochlear nerves. CSF showed elevated protein, lymphocytic pleocytosis, and malignant cells. Serum anti-AQP4 antibodies were positive (1:320), but no other paraneoplastic antibodies were identified. He was diagnosed with LM from lung adenocarcinoma causing secondary BVP via direct infiltration of the vestibulocochlear nerves. Dizziness improved with intrathecal chemotherapy. However, he died approximately one year after discharge. Conclusion BVP may be the initial presentation of LM. It underscores the necessity of considering rare etiologies in patients with unexplained BVP. Early recognition and targeted therapy may improve neurological outcomes, although overall prognosis remains limited in the setting of disseminated malignancy.

papers.abstract: Surgical randomized trials have transformed gynecologic oncology by redefining the extent and route of surgery, nodal assessment, and multimodality care. However, the effect of a surgical trial does not end at publication. Unlike medical therapies, surgical interventions depend on operator expertise, team coordination, pathology support and perioperative infrastructure. Beyond controlled trial settings, these conditions may change, creating technical drift, indication drift, and inequitable adoption. Implementation should therefore be considered a distinct, structured phase of surgical research. The period is particularly vulnerable because landmark trials often evaluate de-escalation or technically complex innovations. Expanding de-escalation beyond trial-tested eligibility can cause undertreatment, whereas diffusion of complex procedures without sufficient expertise or infrastructure can increase morbidity. Disparities in access to specialist surgeons, imaging, pathology, molecular testing, perioperative support, and long-term follow-up amplify these risks. Responsible translation requires trial reports to define the technical, institutional, and patient-selection conditions under which outcomes were achieved. Strategies may include credentialing expectations, operative standards, and risk-appropriate guidelines. Once findings sufficiently resolve equipoise, post-implementation surveillance should determine whether effective procedures are adopted-or ineffective ones abandoned-and whether appropriate use, technical fidelity, safety, equity, and outcomes are maintained as practice spreads. Secondary databases can evaluate utilization, perioperative safety, equity, practice-change attribution, and selected real-world outcomes at scale, but incompletely capture appropriateness, technical fidelity, granular complications, recurrence, and patient-reported quality of life. Surveillance should therefore use a multilevel approach that matches each objective to where information is generated and supplements broad databases with targeted clinical, procedural, and patient-reported data. Treated as an active research phase, surveillance can ensure that surgical innovation reaches the right patients and settings, with outcomes consistent with the supporting evidence.

papers.abstract: This study examined both National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guideline concordance and steroid taper duration with clinical outcomes in patients with gynecologic malignancies experiencing immune-related AEs. This single-institution retrospective cohort included patients with gynecologic malignancies treated with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) from August 2016 to September 2025 who developed grade 3 or 4 immune-related AEs requiring systemic steroids. Clinical and steroid treatment data were abstracted. NCCN guideline concordance and outcomes were assessed. 63 patients contributing 73 steroid tapers were included. Most patients had endometrial (41.3%), cervical (27.0%), or ovarian cancer (23.8%), and pembrolizumab was the most used ICI (74.6%). 46 tapers (63.0%) were NCCN guideline concordant and 27 (37.0%) were NCCN guideline discordant, with discordance most often driven by taper length and premature initiation. 14 (19.2%) were < 28 days, and 59 (80.8%) were ≥ 28 days. NCCN discordant tapers were more likely to require additional supportive medications for irAE management (e.g. secondary steroids) than concordant tapers (81.5% vs 56.2%, p = 0.0300). NCCN concordance was associated with longer time to ICI restart (56 vs 21 days, p = 0.0241). Tapers <28 days were more likely to require additional supportive medications (100% vs 57.6%, p = 0.0027) and steroids (35.7% vs 8.4%, p = 0.0253) than tapers ≥28 days. Tapers ≥28 days were associated with higher rates of ICI discontinuation due to toxicity (59.3% vs 28.6%, p = 0.0381). Rates of hospitalization, ICU admission, and AE resolution did not differ by NCCN concordance or taper duration. Corticosteroid taper practices varied substantially in patients with gynecologic malignancies experiencing severe irAEs; shorter and guideline-discordant tapers were associated with greater treatment escalation and steroid reinitiation.

papers.abstract: Plasma cholesterol is correlated with worse outcomes in breast and ovarian cancer. Prior work indicates that myeloid immune cells are highly responsive to cholesterol metabolism. Interestingly, Liver Receptor Homolog-1 (LRH-1, or NR5A2), a key transcriptional regulator of cholesterol homeostasis is highly expressed in neutrophils and is associated with increased survival time. However, the roles of LRH-1 within neutrophils remain unclear. We therefore focused on how LRH-1 influences neutrophil behaviors relevant to cancer. Small molecule ligands for LRH-1 regulated neutrophil migration towards cancer cells. Phagocytosis was also regulated by LRH-1 ligands, the extent being dependent on type of bait (e. coli vs. cancer cells). In T cell co-cultures, neutrophils pretreated with an LRH-1 agonist promoted greater T cell expansion, particularly in CD4+ cells, while LRH-1 inhibition suppressed this response. NETosis is a known trigger of recurrence from dormancy and subsequent tumor growth. Importantly LRH-1 activation reduced NETosis, while treatment with an antagonist or inverse agonist enhanced NETosis, likely through altered reactive oxygen species. Treatment of mice with an inverse agonist of LRH-1 increased the growth of mammary tumors in a NET-dependent manner. Mice harboring dormant D2.0R mammary cancer lesions treated with an LRH-1 inverse agonist exhibited earlier tumor recurrence and enhanced metastatic progression. In contrast, treatment with BL001, a small chemical LRH-1 agonist, delayed recurrence in D2.0R-grafted mice. These findings reveal that LRH-1 is a novel regulator of neutrophil-driven immune responses within the tumor microenvironment. LRH-1 is thus a promising therapeutic target to suppress the progression of breast and ovarian cancer.

papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is a universal feature of cancer and may arise as early as precancer stages during lung adenocarcinoma evolution, yet the emergence of aggressive transcriptional programs remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomics with single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity across hyperplasia, adenoma, and invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC) in a genetically engineered mouse model (129S4/Sv KrasLSL-G12D/+). Disease progression was accompanied by coordinated remodeling of epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments, along with dynamic changes in proliferation, immune response, and metabolic pathways. Notably, lesions of the same histological stage exhibited substantial transcriptional heterogeneity. By quantifying dedifferentiation states, we identified a subset of adenomas that had already diverged toward highly proliferative and metabolically active programs despite lacking invasive features. These lesions were further marked by early chromosome 6 amplification, whose corresponding human ortholog signature recapitulated aggressive proliferation-associated programs in early-stage human lung adenocarcinoma. Spatial analyses further revealed pronounced intratumoral heterogeneity within IAC, with tumor core regions showing increased proliferation and metabolism but reduced immune signaling compared to peripheral regions. In addition, immune checkpoint gene expression in T cells was transiently elevated at the hyperplasia stage, suggesting early immune modulation prior to overt malignancy. Together, these findings indicate that aggressive transcriptional divergence can emerge early during lung adenocarcinoma evolution and that spatial organization critically shapes tumor and immune programs before and after invasion.

papers.abstract: Cancer-associated adipocytes (CAAs) are increasingly recognized as active and heterogeneous components of the tumor microenvironment. Initially defined as tumor-adjacent adipocytes characterized by lipid depletion, reduced expression of mature adipocyte markers, and inflammatory activation, CAAs are now understood to encompass a spectrum of context-dependent states. These states are shaped by anatomical location, preexisting adipocyte properties, tumor-derived signals, and therapeutic exposure. Through metabolic exchange, paracrine signaling, direct cell contact, extracellular-vesicle communication, and matrix remodeling, CAAs influence tumor-cell plasticity, metastatic colonization, immune dysfunction, stromal organization, and treatment response. In turn, signals from tumor, immune, and stromal cells continuously reshape adipocyte identity and function, placing CAAs within reciprocal multicellular networks. This review examines the evolving criteria used to identify CAAs, their lineage origins and plasticity, their spatial organization, and their interactions with tumor, immune, and stromal compartments. The contribution of CAAs to therapeutic adaptation is also discussed, together with potential intervention points involving CAA-derived outputs and the metabolic dependencies induced in recipient cells. Finally, major methodological challenges are considered. Adipocyte-resolved profiling, lineage tracing, spatial multiomics, lipid flux analysis, and physiologically relevant models will be needed to distinguish transient remodeling from stable state transitions and to identify context-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities.

papers.abstract: AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) is a highly conserved serine/threonine kinase regarded as an indispensable energy sensor during metabolic stress, coordinating diverse biological processes, including glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, mitochondrial dynamics, and multiple stress-responsive signaling pathways. Growing evidence shows that dysregulated AMPK signaling plays closely linked roles in tumorigenesis. Depending on the context, AMPK signaling can suppress or promote tumor growth. Mechanistically, dysregulated AMPK kinase activity contributes to metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial dysfunction, and epigenetic alterations, all recognized hallmarks of cancer. Consequently, targeting AMPK signaling has emerged as a promising strategy for cancer therapy. In this review, we summarize the molecular mechanisms regulating AMPK signaling, discuss its dual functions in tumor biology, highlight recent advances in AMPK-targeted therapeutic strategies, and address current challenges and future perspectives for the clinical translation of AMPK-targeted cancer therapy.

papers.abstract: Background The clinical efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors combined with chemotherapy (± targeted agents) in patients with proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains unclear. This study systematically evaluated the efficacy of this regimen. Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov for relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to May 2026. The primary outcomes were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS); effect sizes were estimated as hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs). Results Six RCTs comprising 1,165 participants were included. The addition of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to chemotherapy, with or without anti-VEGF agents, was associated with prolonged PFS (HR = 0.84, 95%CI [0.73, 0.95], P = 0.007) and OS (HR = 0.83, 95%CI [0.73, 0.94], P = 0.004). Subgroup analyses for PFS preliminarily suggested greater benefit in male patients (HR = 0.77, 95%CI [0.64, 0.94], P = 0.010), those with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 (HR = 0.73, 95%CI [0.56, 0.95], P = 0.018), those with liver metastases (HR = 0.82, 95%CI [0.68, 0.98], P = 0.027), those without prior adjuvant therapy (HR = 0.81, 95%CI [0.67, 0.98], P = 0.030), those with a PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) < 1 (HR = 0.53, 95%CI [0.30, 0.95], P = 0.032), those with synchronous metastases (HR = 0.79, 95%CI [0.63, 0.99], P = 0.037), and those with Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS) mutations (HR = 0.49, 95%CI [0.30, 0.80], P=0.005). These subgroup findings are exploratory, and interaction tests were not performed. Conclusions PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors combined with chemotherapy (with or without targeted agents) may improve the prognosis of patients with pMMR mCRC and represent a potential first-line treatment option. papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming, a key feature of cancer progression that enables tumor adaptation to stress and therapy, represents an emerging target in anticancer research through dietary and pharmacological modulation. Dietary strategies such as caloric restriction (CR), intermittent fasting, and nutrient-specific modifications are emerging approaches to target oncogenic metabolism. Preclinical studies show that CR reduces tumor burden and inhibits IGF-1/mTOR signaling, while restoring immune pathways. Complementary preclinical evidence confirms that pharmacological inhibitors of the IGF-1R and mTOR pathways independently expose metabolic vulnerabilities, while concurrent autophagy blockade alongside mTOR inhibition can further reduce cancer cell viability by preventing stress adaptation. Multi-omics analyses facilitate the identification of how dietary restriction and pharmacological interventions remodel the tumor microenvironment by altering immune infiltration and stromal interactions, and uncover metabolic dependencies, that represent actionable therapeutic vulnerabilities. These findings suggest that dietary and pharmacological metabolic modulation represents an innovative approach in anticancer research. Preclinical models demonstrate the capability of these interventions to suppress tumor growth and enhance therapeutic responses, while early-phase clinical trials currently establish their safety and biological feasibility. In this review, we aim to summarize findings from in vitro models, in vivo animal studies, clinical observations, and multi-omics analyses to assess the potential of diet and pharmacological mimetics in influencing tumor metabolism and the tumor microenvironment.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Evidence of treatment strategies in frail patients (i.e. not fit for combination therapies) with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is limited to dose-reduced doublet regimens or oral fluoropyrimidines (FP) with bevacizumab. We conducted a systematic review analyzing evidence for oral FPs with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-directed monoclonal antibodies for patients with RAS wild-type (WT) mCRC across treatment lines. Methods We searched PubMed and Cochrane Library for phase II and phase III studies evaluating oral FPs (capecitabine, S-1 or trifluridine/tipiracil (FTD/TPI)) plus EGFR-directed monoclonal antibody (panitumumab or cetuximab) in mCRC. Outcomes included efficacy and safety. Results Seven publications met inclusion criteria (n = 262 patients). First-line data was limited to elderly cohorts receiving capecitabine plus cetuximab or panitumumab with a median progression-free survival (PFS)/median overall survival (OS) of 7.2/17.1 months (cetuximab) and 7.5/23.7 months (panitumumab), respectively. In third-line and beyond, median PFS for the combination of FTD/TPI plus cetuximab or panitumumab ranged from 2.4 (cetuximab) to 5.8 months (panitumumab), and OS from 9.8 (cetuximab) to 14.2 months (panitumumab). S-1 plus cetuximab was associated with a median PFS of 5.5 months and OS of 13.6 months. Conclusion While capecitabine should not be used together with anti-EGFR antibodies, FTD/TPI in combination with an EGFR-directed antibody appears feasible, shows promising activity and manageable toxicity profile in RAS WT mCRC potentially offering an alternative for frail patients; prospective trials are needed.

papers.abstract: Exercise is the most common approach to prehabilitation; the optimal exercise interventions to improve postoperative outcomes are unknown. This was a systematic review with network meta-analysis that followed a prespecified protocol (CRD420251034396). Peer-reviewed search strategies were applied from inception to 4 April 2025, to Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), without language restrictions. We included all RCTs of prehabilitation that included at least one exercise intervention (aerobic, strength, pulmonary, or functional exercises) and that reported at least one critical outcome (postoperative complications, length of stay, health-related quality of life, or physical recovery). P-scores were used to rank interventions by their probability of being most beneficial. Best practices, including duplicate review, were followed. Confidence in network meta-analysis informed certainty ratings. We screened 7660 citations, reviewed 1480 full-text articles, and included 96 unique RCTs (N=7396). Combined aerobic, pulmonary, and functional exercise were most likely to reduce complications (P-score 0.94, odds ratio 0.16, 95% CI 0.05-0.60; very low certainty) and length of stay (P-score 0.97, mean difference -3.4 days, 95% CI -5.7 to -1.0; moderate certainty). Combined aerobic and strength exercise was most likely to improve health-related quality of life (P-score 0.93, standardised mean difference 0.67, 95% CI 0.07-1.27; low certainty). No exercise interventions significantly improved physical recovery. The efficacy of exercise prehabilitation interventions may be outcome-specific. Implementation of aerobic and pulmonary exercise prehabilitation may be warranted. Low-risk-of-bias trials are required to confirm or refute available data, which are mostly low certainty.

papers.abstract: While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized treatment of the patients with aero-upper digestive squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs), including esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), only a subset of patients benefit from ICIs, therefore entailing exploration of the mechanisms to regulate treatment responsiveness. POLE, as a subunit of DNA polymerase ε, possesses 3'-5' proofreading activity, and its mutations have been associated with favourable response to ICIs in several solid tumors. However, post-translational modification (PTM) of POLE and its impact on the therapeutic efficacy of ICIs are unknown. Here, this study demonstrates that ubiquitin-like protein 3 (Ubl3), whose expression is markedly downregulated in SCCs, covalently binds to Pole, reduces nuclear Pole levels, triggers DNA damage, and activates cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Notably, Ubl3 modification of Pole significantly primes the local immune microenvironment to mitigate the growth of murine aero-upper digestive SCC cells and boost the efficacy of αPD-1 treatment in vivo. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis further revealed that UBL3 expression is positively correlated with better clinical outcomes in a cohort of ESCC patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with αPD-1. Together, our findings unravel UBL3 modification as a novel PTM mechanism governing subcellular location of POLE and its influence on immunotherapy responsiveness, thus making UBL3 modification as a promising immunomodulatory approach to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in patients with aero-upper digestive SCCs.

papers.abstract: Whether intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) offers measurable clinical benefits over intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) for oropharyngeal cancer remains debated. We pooled data from two phase III randomized trials and one matched cohort study comparing IMPT with IMRT and analyzed disease-control, survival, acute toxicity, and nutritional outcomes. The hazard ratio for locoregional recurrence was 1.37 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.56-3.36, I2 = 0%]; for progression-free survival, 0.90 (95% CI 0.61-1.33, I2 = 0%); and for overall survival, 0.79 (95% CI 0.32-1.98, I2 = 47%). Acute grade 3 dysphagia occurred in 24% of patients receiving IMPT, compared with 40.9% receiving IMRT [risk ratio (RR) 0.65, 95% CI 0.51-0.84, I2 = 0%]. Grade 3 xerostomia or oral/pharyngeal dryness occurred in 19.9% and 32.5%, respectively (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.54-0.95, I2 = 0%). Exploratory nutritional outcomes showed no definitive benefit, including 12-month gastrostomy dependence (RR 0.32, 95% CI 0.08-1.28, I2 = 0%), weight loss ≥20% (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.12-9.38, I2 = 85.7%), and composite nutritional endpoints (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.12-7.07, I2 = 87.7%). IMPT's primary advantage is reducing acute toxicity, not improving efficacy.

papers.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has demonstrated substantial clinical benefit in patients with advanced human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive and HER2-low breast cancer. However, treatment-related adverse events-particularly interstitial lung disease (ILD) or pneumonitis-represent a clinically relevant limitation. While UGT1A1 polymorphisms influence toxicity with other topoisomerase I inhibitor-based therapies, their role in T-DXd-related toxicity appears limited. The PROCURE project aimed to investigate germline pharmacogenetic variants beyond UGT1A1 associated with T-DXd-induced ILD. The PROCURE project is a multicenter translational study conducted across 26 Spanish institutions. Germline DNA from patients with advanced HER2-positive or HER2-low breast cancer treated with T-DXd was genotyped using the Infinium Global Diversity Array enriched for pharmacogenomic variants. A candidate gene approach was applied to 14 genes involved in drug metabolism, transport, pharmacodynamics, and immune-mediated drug hypersensitivity. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations with ILD/pneumonitis. A total of 290 patients with clinical and genotyping data were included in the analysis. The median age was 58 years (range, 34-94 years). After a median follow-up of 18.3 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 15.4-20.5], the cohort registered 33 ILD cases (incidence of 11.4%). The strongest association signals mapped to variants within the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) region, with the top single nucleotide polymorphism near HLA-F (rs9258213; OR 6.8, 95% CI 2.6-17.9, P = 9.5 × 10-5). Additional associations were observed in SLCO1B1 and CYP3A4, genes involved in T-DXd transport and metabolism. This study identifies host genetic variation within the HLA locus and drug pharmacokinetic pathways as potential contributors to T-DXd-induced ILD in patients with advanced breast cancer. Although no definitive pharmacogenomic predictor was identified, these findings provide insights into the biological mechanisms underlying this toxicity and support further investigation of pharmacogenomic biomarkers to improve risk stratification and guide personalized T-DXd therapy.

papers.abstract: Biomarker-guided antibiotic protocols using daily procalcitonin or C-reactive protein have been proposed to optimise antibiotic duration in sepsis. This pre-planned process evaluation of the ADAPT-Sepsis trial examined delivery and clinician adherence to procalcitonin- and C-reactive protein-guided protocols. An embedded descriptive process evaluation was conducted within the multicentre ADAPT-Sepsis trial including 2760 adults across 41 UK critical care units. Patients were assigned to procalcitonin-guided, C-reactive protein-guided or standard care. Algorithm-generated recommendations (strong stop, suggest stop or standard care) were relayed to research staff and clinicians who remained blinded to group allocation. Adherence was defined as stopping biomarker sampling after advice. Advice timings, frequencies, adherence rates and reasons for non-adherence were recorded and analysed. Among 2760 patients, strong stop advice occurred earlier in those allocated to the procalcitonin-guided group compared with the C-reactive protein-guided group (mean difference -1.7 days, 95%CI -2.5 to -0.9, p < 0.001). C-reactive protein guidance generated a higher proportion of standard care advice (mean difference -9.1%, 95%CI -10.9% to -7.3%, p < 0.001). Overall advice adherence was greater in patients allocated to the C-reactive protein group than those allocated to the procalcitonin group (mean difference -6.8%, 95%CI -9.0 to -4.5, p < 0.001), driven by the higher proportion of standard care advice and later stronger stop advice with higher adherence (mean difference -14.3%, 95%CI -21.8 to -6.8, p < 0.001). Reasons for advice non-adherence included fixed-duration microbiology guidance, illness severity, continuing fever and elevation of routine inflammatory markers, which did not differ between groups. A C-reactive protein-guided discontinuation protocol achieved higher clinician adherence, probably because its recommendations aligned more closely with established prescribing norms. In contrast, procalcitonin guidance produced earlier and more frequent stop signals, offering greater potential to reduce antibiotic exposure but requiring clinicians to accept earlier discontinuation than usual practice.

papers.abstract: Pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning during laparoscopic colorectal surgery promote atelectasis and increase the risk of postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs). Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) enables individualised PEEP titration by visualising regional lung collapse, facilitating lung-protective ventilation. However, evidence of its effect on clinical PPCs remains limited. In this single-centre, parallel-group RCT, adults with intermediate to high risk for PPCs (ARISCAT score ≥26) who underwent laparoscopic colorectal surgery were randomly assigned to receive intraoperative PEEP titration guided by EIT or a conventional fixed PEEP of 5 cm H2O. The primary outcome was PPCs incidence within 30 days, as determined by a multidisciplinary adjudication team using standardised criteria. Among the 117 randomised participants (mean [range] age: 62 [37-80] yr; 37% female), EIT-guided PEEP (n=59) resulted in lower driving pressure (16 [15-18] cm H2O) compared with fixed PEEP (n=58; 19 [17-22] cm H2O; P<0.0001). The incidence of 30 day PPCs was lower among participants randomised to EIT-guided PEEP (29/59 [49.2%]) than those in the fixed-PEEP group (42/58 [72.4%]; hazard ratio: 0.53; 95% CI, 0.33-0.85; P=0.009). PPCs including atelectasis and pneumonia occurred less frequently among participants randomised to EIT-guided PEEP. Compared with conventional fixed PEEP of 5 cm H2O, EIT-guided PEEP was associated with a lower incidence of PPCs among patients at intermediate to high PPCs risk undergoing laparoscopic colorectal surgery, suggesting a role for EIT in intraoperative lung protection. papers.abstract: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is associated with myocardial injury, acute kidney injury, perioperative stroke, and 30-day mortality. Deep learning (DL) refers to a family of machine-learning methods that learn multiple levels of data representation through nonlinear transformations. In perioperative monitoring, DL models can learn patterns from time-varying physiological signals and combine them with clinical variables to estimate impending IOH risk. DL algorithms applied to continuous physiological waveforms therefore represent a rapidly expanding paradigm for early IOH prediction, but their pooled diagnostic accuracy has not been synthesised within a unified diagnostic-accuracy framework. To quantify the pooled diagnostic accuracy of DL-based IOH prediction models and to identify factors that modify their performance. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through March 2026. Methodological quality was appraised with PROBAST+AI and certainty of evidence with GRADE. A bivariate random-effects model generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and SROC-AUC; heterogeneity was quantified by τ2(Se), τ2(Sp), and ρ. Subgroup analyses (prediction window, DL architecture, modality, IOH reference, analysis unit) and random-effects meta-regression were performed. Twelve studies were included; nine contributed 22 validation datasets. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% CI 0.73-0.81), specificity 0.88 (0.82-0.92), and SROC-AUC 0.87 (0.83-0.90); diagnostic odds ratio 24.7 (16.1-37.9), positive likelihood ratio 6.31, negative likelihood ratio 0.26. Heterogeneity was τ2(Se) = 0.25, τ2(Sp) = 1.04, ρ = -0.28. The 5-min window achieved the highest performance (sensitivity 0.81; specificity 0.91). Meta-regression identified DL architecture as the only significant moderator of specificity (P = 0.02), with hybrid CNN-RNN exceeding pure CNN (β = 1.77, 95% CI 0.45-3.09). Deeks' test was non-significant (P = 0.06). GRADE certainty was Low. DL models for IOH prediction achieve moderate diagnostic accuracy, with hybrid CNN-RNN architectures and 5-min prediction windows showing the most favourable performance. Universal absence of formal calibration assessment, scarce external validation, and geographic concentration constrain immediate clinical translation. papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The 2021 World Health Organization Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (WHO CNS5) integrates histological and molecular criteria for adult diffuse gliomas, but comprehensive molecular testing may be difficult to implement in resource-limited settings. This study assessed the feasibility of a sequential, marker-based approach for diagnostic reassessment and described its association with clinical characteristics and overall survival (OS) in adults from Colombia. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 68 adults with diffuse gliomas treated at two referral hospitals in Bogotá, Colombia, between 2015 and 2023. Molecular assessment used IHC, FISH, PCR, and Sanger sequencing according to the available tissue and diagnostic workflow. The study did not include comprehensive NGS or systematic assessment of combined whole-chromosome 7 gain/chromosome 10 loss (+7/−10). Results: The diagnosis changed after molecular reassessment in 51.5% of cases. The proportion classified as glioblastoma increased from 48.5% under the historical histologic classification to 66.2% under the WHO CNS5-based algorithm, whereas FISH-defined oligodendrogliomas decreased from 17.6% to 11.8%. OS differed among historical histologic groups (p = 0.03), but not among the WHO CNS5-based groups (p = 0.13). Female sex was associated with longer OS in unadjusted analysis (p = 0.02), while age was the only independent predictor in the multivariable analysis. Conclusions: Sequential molecular reassessment materially changed diagnostic categorization in this cohort and was feasible using locally available marker-based methods. However, the results are exploratory, limited by small molecular subgroups, incomplete molecular coverage, and the retrospective treatment context; they should not be interpreted as demonstrating improved treatment selection or survival after reclassification.

papers.abstract: Background: Peptides that selectively bind to cancer-associated proteins are attractive candidates for molecular imaging and targeted therapeutic applications. The urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR) represents a promising molecular target as it is highly expressed in several cancers and has been linked to cancer aggressiveness, invasion, and metastasis. This study applied an NGS-informed biopanning strategy against uPAR, combined with multi-assay downstream validation, to identify and prioritize candidate peptides. Methods: An optimized biopanning protocol incorporating additional selection controls was combined with next-generation sequencing to identify candidate uPAR-binding peptides from a phage display library. Selected peptides were evaluated using complementary in vitro assays, including flow cytometry and a quantitative plate assay. Results: Three peptide candidates were identified and selected for further evaluation with complementary in vitro assays. The optimized workflow incorporates measures to reduce, but not eliminate, enrichment of target-unrelated peptides, and includes complementary validation of the peptides in in vitro assays. Differences observed between the validation methods highlighted the importance of evaluating peptide candidates using complementary assays. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the value of combining an optimized phage display selection with next-generation sequencing and complementary validation assays for identifying candidate peptides. The identified peptides represent promising candidates for further optimization toward molecular imaging and targeted therapeutic applications.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver malignancy, often arising in cirrhosis. Its early non-invasive diagnosis and prognostic assessment remain challenging due to the limited availability of reliable circulating biomarkers, creating the need to establish non-invasive biomarkers that distinguish malignant transformation. This preliminary study aimed to: discover EV-associated miRNAs that differ among healthy subjects, patients with liver cirrhosis, and patients with HCC; validate selected candidates by ddPCR in an independent cohort; compare their abundance in plasma-derived EVs, whole plasma, and paired tumoral/peritumoral tissues; and explore their diagnostic performance for HCC versus cirrhosis and their associations with clinical outcomes. Methods: miRNA sequencing was performed on plasma-derived EVs from an exploratory cohort of 10 healthy subjects, 10 cirrhotic patients, and 10 HCC patients. Three candidate miRNAs, miR-98-5p, miR-130a-3p, and miR-1246, were subsequently quantified by droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) in an independent cohort of 29 HCC patients, 30 cirrhotic patients, and 20 healthy subjects using plasma-derived EVs, plasma, and paired tumoral/peritumoral liver tissues. Results: In plasma EVs, miR-98-5p and miR-130a-3p were reduced in HCC and cirrhotic patients compared with healthy subjects, whereas miR-1246 was increased in HCC compared with cirrhosis. In plasma, all three miRNAs were elevated in HCC compared with cirrhosis and healthy controls. Plasma miR-1246 showed the highest diagnostic performance to discriminate HCC from cirrhosis (AUC = 0.87). In tissue, miR-98-5p was upregulated and miR-130a-3p downregulated in tumoral versus peritumoral samples, whereas miR-1246 showed no significant difference. Higher plasma miR-130a-3p and miR-1246 levels were associated with improved overall survival, while increased miR-98-5p levels were associated with lower relapse rates. Conclusions: Among the three miRNAs, plasma miR-1246 showed the strongest diagnostic performance for distinguishing HCC from liver cirrhosis. Combination with miR-98-5p and/or miR-130a-3p did not improve discrimination. Thus, plasma miR-1246 emerged as the leading candidate diagnostic indicator in the HCC cohort, whereas the three miRNAs showed distinct potential associations with prognosis.

papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has overtaken viral hepatitis as the fastest-growing cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in most high-income countries. What makes this epidemic clinically treacherous is a feature that distinguishes MASLD-related HCC from other aetiologies: roughly half of all cases arise in livers that have never progressed to cirrhosis, slipping through the net of conventional surveillance strategies. The molecular journey from fatty liver to malignancy unfolds through at least six interlocking programmes: lipotoxic rewiring of hepatocyte metabolism, including acquired lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) dysfunction, oncogenic glucose reprogramming through the p53-PUMA-mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) axis, and a preliminary MLKL-Mfn2 axis linking metabolic stress to mitochondrial dysfunction; a chronic shift in the hepatic immune milieu toward tumour-permissive tolerance; gut microbiota dysbiosis flooding portal circulation with pro-inflammatory metabolites; progressive collapse of autophagic flux with p62/SQSTM1 accumulation and lipolysosome formation; and pervasive epigenetic rewriting spanning DNA methylation, novel histone marks, and non-coding RNA networks. We also discuss emerging biomarkers and therapeutic strategies, closing with a brief note on Doublecortin-like kinase 1 (DCLK1) as a candidate marker at the intersection of cancer stem cell identity and immune microenvironment subversion.

papers.abstract: Epigenetic therapies can reverse malignant transcriptional programs, but their activity is often constrained by adaptive stress responses that allow cancer cells to survive and recover. Autophagy is a central component of this adaptation. By sustaining metabolic homeostasis, mitochondrial fitness, proteostasis, and lysosomal recycling, autophagy can buffer the cellular injury produced by inhibitors of DNA methyltransferases, histone deacetylases, and bromodomain proteins. These observations provide a strong rationale for combining epigenetic therapies with autophagy inhibition. However, the field has too often equated autophagosome accumulation with increased autophagic flux and treatment-induced autophagy with a functional dependency. Moreover, the lysosomotropic agents used in early clinical studies incompletely inhibit autophagy and exert broader effects on lysosomal biology. Consequently, compelling preclinical activity has not translated into consistent clinical benefit. Here, we critically evaluate the mechanisms through which epigenetic therapies engage autophagy, distinguish correlative markers from causal evidence of resistance, and assess the preclinical and clinical data supporting combination strategies. We also define the major barriers to translation, including inadequate pharmacodynamic assays, a lack of predictive biomarkers, context-dependent effects on tumor and immune cells, and the limited potency and selectivity of current autophagy inhibitors. Defining when, where, and how autophagy becomes a targetable dependency will be essential to translate this compelling biology into an effective precision treatment.

papers.abstract: As research in molecular biology continues to advance, the classification of endometrial cancer has gradually shifted from traditional histology toward risk stratification based on the integration of molecular subtyping with clinicopathologic factors. Molecular subtyping has not only transformed our understanding of the biological heterogeneity of endometrial cancer but also provided new evidence for prognostic assessment and treatment selection. However, the maturity of clinical evidence and the translational therapeutic value vary across molecular subtypes. This review systematically summarizes the molecular characteristics and clinical significance of the POLE ultramutated(POLE-mut)subtype, mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) subtype, p53 abnormal (p53-abn) subtype, and no specific molecular profile (NSMP) subtype, with a focus on evaluating whether different molecular features can be further translated from risk stratification into specific treatment decisions. Centering on key issues such as de-escalated therapy for the POLE-mut subtype, the predictive value of immunotherapy for the dMMR subtype, intensified therapy for the p53-abn subtype, and further risk stratification of the NSMP subtype, this review analyzes the clinical basis and limitations of existing evidence and further discusses the challenges that tumors with multiple molecular features pose for classification and treatment decision making. Building on this, the paper compares how major international guidelines integrate molecular information with clinical and pathologic factors and analyzes real world implementation barriers such as testing standardization, result interpretation, and healthcare accessibility. Finally, it outlines the potential value of emerging technologies, including liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence, and multiomics, in dynamic risk assessment and precision therapy. This review aims to trace the continuum of evidence from molecular discovery to clinical action, clarifying which clinical decisions can be supported by existing molecular markers and identifying questions that current evidence cannot yet answer, thereby providing guidance for the precise application and clinical translation of molecular subtyping in endometrial cancer.

papers.abstract: Availability of clinical trials for prostate cancer in the US varies greatly by region. County-level analyses are vital to characterize healthcare access, disease burden, and population-level disparities. Utilizing the ClinicalTrials.gov trial database, we collated all interventional prostate cancer trials between June 1, 2019, and June 1, 2025. We compiled data on county characteristics along with Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) designations derived from the CDC, NCI, and the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry data. A zero-inflated negative binomial regression model was used to evaluate trial availability. Trial characteristics were summarized using descriptive analysis. We found 884 eligible trials. Among 3,145 counties, only 631 had at least one clinical trial over the study period. Most trials (51%) included patients with metastatic disease. Sixteen percent of trials investigated curative treatments, while 65% examined palliative interventions. The majority of studies (52.5%) had funding from pharmaceutical companies. There was no significant relationship between trial availability and incidence or mortality rates. Among counties with at least one trial, those with a low SVI had twice as many trials per household when compared to those with high SVI (IRR 2.05, 95% CI 1.54 - 2.74, p<0.001). Counties with no trials were more rural (72.3% vs 22.0%) and had fewer specialist physicians (17.1% vs 69.1%). Prostate cancer trials are disproportionately concentrated in the US, with lower representation in vulnerable areas. Expanding trial access to underserved areas is a crucial step in promoting equitable access to care.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma represents the most aggressive primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system, characterized by extensive intratumoral heterogeneity, profound immunosuppression, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes. Although immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, its clinical efficacy in GBM remains limited, largely due to the complexity of the tumor ecosystem and the lack of validated predictive biomarkers. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational approaches have provided unprecedented opportunities to decipher tumor heterogeneity and identify clinically actionable biomarkers. This mini-review integrates studies related to scRNA-seq and its combination technology, further elaborating on the tumor plasticity, immune suppression, and metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming mechanisms of GBM. The article systematically summarizes the complete analysis process of integrating single-cell multi-omics data by AI and highlights the application value of AI in validating biomarkers. The above research ideas are expected to overcome clinical resistance problems, optimize patient stratification schemes, and enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy, providing theoretical support for developing highly stable prognostic biomarkers and achieving individualized precise immunotherapy for glioblastoma.

papers.abstract: Brain metastases (BM) incidence and characteristics remain poorly defined due to registry data being often incomplete, recording only primary tumors or unspecified metastases. The objective of this study was to examine BM incidence rates and characteristics confirmed by MRI in North Savo, Finland. In this retrospective study, North Savo residents with first MRI diagnosis of BM between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2023 were identified through the radiology information system, irrespective of primary cancer diagnosis date. Medical and histopathological records were reviewed. Population person-years were estimated by summing annual end-year counts of all North Savo residents obtained from Statistics Finland. Crude incidence rates and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs), standardized to the 2013 European Standard population, were calculated. Temporal trends were assessed using age-adjusted Poisson regression. Among 516 patients, 474 had histopathological verification. Cancers originating from lung and breast tissue accounted for 56.8% of BM cases. Overall crude incidence was 10.22 (95% CI 9.36-11.15) and ASIR was 9.20 (95% CI 8.42-10.04) per 100,000 person years. ASIR increased from 5.8 in 2004-2008 to 11.8 in 2019-2023. Age-adjusted Poisson regression estimated a 24% increase in incidence per five-year period (incidence rate ratio 1.24; 95% CI 1.14-1.34; P < 0.001). Age-specific incidence peaked at 33.1 per 100,000 person years among patients aged 70-74 years. MRI-confirmed BM incidence increased over 20 years, despite age standardization. Incidence was highest among older adults. These findings provide contemporary population-based epidemiological data of BM incidence.

papers.abstract: Brain metastases (BM) are frequent in EGFR-mutated (EGFRm) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and remain challenging after prior EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This exploratory study evaluated high-dose fimmonertinib and explored subtype-specific spatial biology. iFORCE was a prospective, single-center, single-arm study. Eligible patients had advanced NSCLC harboring EGFR mutations with previously treated BM following EGFR-TKI therapy, or intracranial disease progression. Patients received 160 mg firmonertinib once daily. The primary endpoint was intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS). Archival paired primary tumors and BM specimens from an independent retrospective cohort underwent exploratory digital spatial profiling (DSP). Twenty-three patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 19.7 months (95% CI, 14.5-25.3), median iPFS was 14.6 months (95% CI, 4.2-not estimable [NE]), with 12- and 18-month iPFS rates of 53.8% and 46.1%, respectively. Based on the best intracranial overall response, intracranial objective response and disease control rates were 34.8% (95% CI, 16.4-57.3) and 91.3% (95% CI, 72.0-98.9). Median systemic PFS was 10.7 months (95% CI, 3.9-NE). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 13 (56.5%) patients, mostly grade 1; one patient (4.3%) developed grade 3 stomatitis. No treatment discontinuations or treatment-related deaths were observed. DSP revealed distinct EGFR subtype-specific BM ecosystems: exon 19 deletion tumors retained immune-enriched inflammatory programs, whereas L858R-mutated tumors showed tumor-intrinsic cell-cycle, DNA-repair, RNA-splicing, apoptosis-resistance, and immune-evasion features. Fimonertinib 160 mg showed promising intracranial activity with a manageable safety profile in EGFR-TKI-treated EGFRm NSCLC with BM. L858R BM displayed tumor-intrinsic, microenvironment-independent biology, suggesting preferential sensitivity to high-dose firmonertinib.

papers.abstract: Background: Patients with cancer often require hospital-level care to address urgent needs and symptom concerns. However, little research has sought to identify patient factors, particularly rural-urban residence, associated with care outcomes in this population. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including adult patients with cancer admitted to the University of Oklahoma Medical Center from January 2017 through December 2022. We extracted patients’ sociodemographic (ie, age, sex, race, ethnicity, rural-urban residence [Rural-Urban Continuum Codes]) and clinical (ie, Charlson comorbidity index [CCI] score, cancer type, metastatic disease status) information from the electronic health record. We used multivariable models to explore associations of patient factors with clinical outcomes (time to hospital discharge for length of stay [LOS], time to first readmission, and time to death [overall survival]). Results: We identified 20,683 patients in our cohort (mean [SD] age, 62.6 [15.4] years; 52% female sex, 40% with a CCI score ≥3, 41% with metastatic cancer, 31% with nonmetropolitan residence). Median hospital LOS was 4.0 days, with 30- and 90-day readmission rates of 15% and 23%, and median survival was 5.0 years. Older age (hazard ratio [HR], 0.93; P <.001), male sex (HR, 0.94; P <.001), higher comorbidity (CCI score ≥3: HR, 0.70; P <.001), and metastatic disease (HR, 0.88; P <.001) were associated with longer LOS. Higher comorbidity (CCI score ≥3: HR, 2.70; P <.001) was associated with a greater risk of readmission. Older age (HR, 1.50; P <.001), CCI score ≥3 (HR, 1.68; P <.001), and nonmetropolitan residence (HR, 1.08; P =.007) were associated with worse survival. Conclusions: In this cohort of hospitalized patients with cancer, we identified associations of patients’ sociodemographic and clinical factors with their hospital LOS, risk of readmission, and survival. Findings from this work could help inform targeted efforts to enhance care delivery and outcomes for this population.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer patients from neighboring Hawaiian Islands face challenges including limited access to specialists and geographic isolation. Surgical delays longer than 8 weeks from diagnosis can negatively impact survival. Time from diagnosis to surgery (TTS) and predictors of delay are unknown for this population. Retrospective chart review was performed on breast cancer patients from neighboring Hawaiian Islands who underwent upfront surgery on O'ahu categorized as TTS of 8 weeks or longer. Demographic and clinical characteristics were evaluated. Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical analyses. Binary logistic regression adjusted for confounding variables. The study reviewed 221 breast cancer patients (2014-2024) from neighboring Hawaiian Islands. The mean TTS was 9.4 weeks. In the univariate analysis, TTS longer than 8 weeks was associated with post-pandemic diagnosis versus during and before the pandemic (41.8 vs. 16.3 vs. 418%), preoperative diagnostic testing compared with no testing (79.6 vs. 20.4%), plastic surgery consultation compared with no consultation (51.0 vs. 49.0%,), and mastectomy compared with breast-conserving surgery (61.2 vs. 37.8%) (all p < 0.005). Multivariate analysis showed post-pandemic diagnosis (odds ratio [OR], 2.84; 95% CI, 1.15-7.00; p = 0.023), time from biopsy to consultation (OR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.13-1.56; p < 0.001), and preoperative diagnostic testing (OR, 3.22; 95% CI, 1.27-8.16; p = 0.014) as significant predictors of TTS longer than 8 weeks. Nearly half of neighboring Hawaiian Islands breast cancer patients experienced delay in surgery. Streamlining preoperative management could meaningfully shorten the time from biopsy to surgery and improve access to care and outcomes for this population.

papers.abstract: To investigate the performance of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for diagnosing tumor thrombus (TT) and predicting response to pembrolizumab and axitinib in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with TT. We reviewed RCC patients who underwent contrast-enhanced CT, mpMRI, and 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT. Diagnostic performance for detecting TT was analyzed, with TT confirmed by experienced pathologists. We further analyzed clear cell RCC (ccRCC) patients with TT who received pembrolizumab and axitinib and evaluated imaging features for predicting therapeutic efficacy by using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations). Model calibration was assessed with the Hosmer-Lemeshow test. A total of 166 RCC patients were initially included, of whom 56 had TT. 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT showed higher overall diagnostic performance for TT than contrast-enhanced CT and mpMRI, with incremental detection primarily observed for Mayo level 0-I TT. The sensitivity and specificity of PET/CT in diagnosing TT were 0.96 (95% CI 0.88-0.99) and 0.97 (95% CI 0.92-0.99), respectively. Then, 35 ccRCC patients with TT underwent an average of 5 cycles of pembrolizumab and axitinib, followed by surgery. Following neoadjuvant therapy, 21 patients exhibited a partial response, while 14 showed nonresponse. TT SUVmax demonstrated significant predictive value for response to neoadjuvant therapy, with an AUC of 0.80 (95% CI 0.63-0.92; bootstrap-corrected, 0.79). The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated adequate calibration (P > 0.05). 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT may provide incremental value for detecting low-level TT and shows potential for predicting response to pembrolizumab plus axitinib in RCC. However, the clinical significance of detecting early TT remains uncertain.

papers.abstract: Early detection of melanoma remains challenging, and minimally invasive diagnostic tools are needed to complement imaging and histopathology. Circulating tumour antigen-specific antibodies (Abs) are promising biomarkers, but their diagnostic value across melanoma stages is not fully established. Circulating IgG and IgM Abs were profiled in plasma from two independent melanoma cohorts, early-stage (n = 65) and advanced-stage (n = 77), alongside healthy controls (n = 86) and individuals with prior cancer in remission (n = 37). A protein microarray containing 263 tumour antigens, predominantly cancer-testis (CT) antigens, was used to measure plasma antibody (Ab) reactivity. Univariate and multivariate ROC analyses identified candidate diagnostic biomarker signatures. Early-stage melanoma was best distinguished by an IgM signature comprising AURKA, BAGE3, BAGE4, CDK7, CEP290, MYBL2, PIAS2, RAD51 and SPANXB1 (AUC = 0.939). An IgG signature including ANKRD45, BCL2L14, CDK2, MAGEA4v3, MAPK3 and RBM46 achieved AUC = 0.827. Advanced-stage melanoma exhibited broader Ab repertoires, including an IgG signature (CTAG1A, DKKL1, PIWIL2, SPANXN1, TSGA10, TSPY1; AUC = 0.865) and an IgM signature (CPXCR1, CSAG2, FMR1NB, FOXR2, LIPI, MAGEA5, TSGA10; AUC = 0.889). Individuals in cancer remission displayed persistent Ab signatures distinct from early melanoma and healthy controls. Overlap between IgG and IgM repertoires was minimal, highlighting complementary discriminatory value. Circulating IgG and IgM Abs against tumour antigens reveal stage-specific signatures that distinguish melanoma from healthy individuals and those in cancer remission, identifying candidate discovery-stage diagnostic biomarker signatures warranting independent validation in larger prospective cohorts to determine clinical utility.

papers.abstract: Historically viewed as a localized gastrointestinal malignancy, colorectal cancer (CRC) is increasingly recognized as a systemic pathology that actively programs distant microenvironments. This review delineates a novel mechanistic framework wherein CRC-driven dysregulation of the brain-gut-microbiota axis (BGMA) acts as a systemic architect of the breast pre-metastatic niche (PMN). We synthesize how localized intestinal oncogenic stress propagates through three convergent conduits: (1) Immune Reprogramming, where gut-derived inflammatory mediators and extracellular vesicles (EVs) recruit myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) to the mammary stroma; (2) Neuro-ecological Conditioning, involving chronic hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activation and sympathetic hyperactivation that drives catecholamine-mediated remodeling of breast tissue; and (3) Humoral-Metabolic Convergence, specifically via the "estrobolome" and secondary bile acids that synchronize systemic hormonal levels with local tissue receptivity. By reframing CRC progression as a systemic pathology that potentially preconditions distant, hormone-sensitive environments, we propose the BGMA as a conceptual framework for prospective "systemic interception", outlining roadmaps to neutralize metastatic cascades at their incipient, reversible stages.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors such as anti-PD-1 antibodies are essential in cancer therapy. Emerging data suggest that lower doses may be effective and more economical, though further evidence is needed. We conducted a retrospective study at Centre Léon Bérard to assess the efficacy and safety of low-dose nivolumab (20 mg every 3 weeks) in patients with advanced cancer, mainly squamous cell carcinomas (SCC). Between 2023 and 2024, 53 patients were treated, with a median age of 74 years; 39.6% were over 80. Most were male (64%) and had ECOG ≥ 2 (69.9%). Primary tumor sites included cutaneous SCC (34%), head and neck SCC (32%), and soft tissue sarcoma (15%). After a median follow-up of 8.3 months, median overall survival was 7.5 months. The objective response rate (ORR) was 20.8%, driven by the SCC subgroup; no responses were observed in non-SCC histologies, in patients with prior ICI exposure, or beyond the second line of treatment. Among IO-naïve SCC patients treated in first or second line (n = 22), ORR was 50%. Toxicity was manageable: 18.7% experienced immune-related adverse events, with only 3.7% grade 3. Low-dose nivolumab demonstrates encouraging efficacy and tolerability in a frail population, supporting its potential role in resource-limited settings. Prospective trials are warranted to confirm these findings in broader populations.

papers.abstract: Angiogenesis is a major driver of tumor progression and a validated therapeutic target in highly vascularized cancers such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma. However, the clinical benefit of antivascular endothelial growth factor therapies is limited by the emergence of resistance. We identified a vascular endothelial growth factor A splice variant, termed Lymphatic and Vascular Resistance Factor (LVRF), which promotes both angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis and is upregulated following anti‐angiogenic treatment. To therapeutically target this pathway, we generated fully human monoclonal antibodies against LVRF. Lead antibodies displayed high specificity and nanomolar affinity and effectively inhibited LVRF‐driven biological activities. Anti‐LVRF antibodies reduced renal carcinoma cell invasion, inhibited vascular and lymphatic endothelial responses, and suppressed lymphatic endothelial cell sprouting. In vivo , treatment significantly reduced the growth of bevacizumab‐resistant renal carcinoma xenografts, induced regression of blood and lymphatic vessels, and decreased metastatic dissemination in zebrafish models. These findings identify LVRF as a mediator of resistance to anti‐angiogenic therapy and support therapeutic targeting of LVRF as a novel strategy for vascularized tumors resistant to current antivascular endothelial growth factor treatments.

papers.abstract: This study examined whether the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and whether this association differs from that of absolute ICU admission glucose. This single-center retrospective study included 731 surgical episodes from 709 adults who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. SHR was calculated as the first ICU glucose divided by HbA1c-derived estimated average glucose. The primary outcome was an unweighted composite of 30-day mortality, stroke, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 3 acute kidney injury, reoperation for bleeding, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and deep sternal wound infection. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinically relevant covariates. The composite outcome occurred in 90 surgical episodes (12.3%). SHR was associated with the composite outcome after adjustment (odds ratio [OR], 1.103 per 0.1 increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.008-1.208; P = 0.033), whereas ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated (OR, 1.019 per 10 mg/dL increase; 95% CI 0.946-1.096; P = 0.626). SHR at ICU admission was associated with major postoperative complications in the primary analysis, whereas absolute ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated after multivariable adjustment. Confidence intervals for SHR included 1.0 in several sensitivity analyses. SHR warrants prospective evaluation as an early postoperative risk marker after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have limited efficacy in estrogen receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (ER+/HER2-) breast cancer, and the mechanisms underlying immune resistance remain unclear. The androgen receptor gene (AR), expressed in a substantial proportion of ER-positive tumors, has been implicated in tumor biology; however, its role in the tumor immune microenvironment and immunotherapy response is not well understood. We investigated the association between AR expression, transcriptome-derived immune cell-associated signatures, and response to ICIs in 4046 patients with breast cancer across five cohorts with bulk transcriptomic data and two cohorts with single-cell transcriptomic data. High AR expression was consistently associated with reduced transcriptome-derived tumor-infiltrating leukocyte scores across multiple ER+/HER2- cohorts. Specifically, signatures associated with cluster of differentiation (CD)-8+ T-cell subsets, dendritic cells, and M1 macrophages were significantly reduced in AR-high tumors, indicating a transcriptionally immune-suppressed tumor microenvironment. In the I-SPY2 cohort, AR-high tumors demonstrated significantly lower pathological complete response rates after neoadjuvant ICI therapy. Furthermore, AR expression showed a predictive performance for ICI response that was superior to that with programmed cell death protein-1 and programmed cell death ligand-1 (area under the curve 0.82 vs. 0.73 and 0.60, respectively). Interestingly, single-cell analysis revealed that AR expression across multiple cell types, including epithelial, endothelial, and myeloid, was associated with reduced ICI responsiveness. Additionally, AR inhibition using enzalutamide was associated with increased signatures associated with CD8+ T cells, dendritic cells, and M1 macrophages. These findings suggest that AR expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and reduced response to ICIs in ER+/HER2- breast cancer.

papers.abstract: To develop and validate a risk prediction model for postpartum urinary retention (PUR) among parturients receiving epidural analgesia (EA) during vaginal delivery, to support individualized bladder management. This dual-center retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic medical records from two hospitals (2022-2024). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to select independent predictors from demographic, labor, and analgesia-related variables. A clinical nomogram was developed. The model underwent internal and external validation; performance was assessed using calibration, discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]), and decision curve analysis (DCA). Among 1019 parturients receiving EA (PUR incidence 16.09%), prolonged analgesia duration and prolonged second-stage labor were independently associated with PUR, whereas higher intermittent catheterization frequency (ICF) was associated with a lower rate of recorded PUR. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination, satisfactory calibration, and clinical net benefit across validation cohorts. The validated nomogram provides real-time, individualized estimates of PUR risk during late labor. By identifying parturients at elevated risk, it offers an evidence-based basis for risk-adaptive bladder monitoring and individualized care; however, whether such model-guided management ultimately reduces PUR incidence remains to be established in prospective interventional studies.
